title: Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom tendrá anime: esta madrastra no quiere ser malvada
summary: Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom anuncia su anime para televisión. El webtoon coreano reinventa Blancanieves con una madrastra que solo quiere cuidar a su hijastra.
details: Anime Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom tendrá anime: esta madrastra no quiere ser malvada El popular webtoon coreano reinventa Blancanieves con una reina que solo quiere ganarse el cariño de su hijastra. Mirukaru hace 35 minutos 0 Comentarios ADS Todos conocemos la historia de Blancanieves y su terrible madrastra, pero ¿qué pasaría si aquella reina malvada solamente quisiera consentir a su hijastra? Esa es la peculiar premisa de Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom , el popular webtoon coreano que recibirá una adaptación al anime para televisión . El anuncio llegó acompañado de una primera imagen promocional y confirma que esta historia de reencarnación, romance y problemas familiares finalmente dará el salto a la animación japonesa. La noticia fue revelada el 19 de noviembre de 2026 por Kakao Piccoma, que confirmó la producción del anime mediante su cuenta oficial en X. La adaptación utilizará el título japonés Mamahaha dakedo Musume ga Kawaisugiru , que podría traducirse como «Soy su madrastra, pero mi hija es demasiado adorable». El anuncio también coincide con el quinto aniversario de la publicación del webtoon en Piccoma. Para celebrarlo, la plataforma compartió una ilustración promocional que presenta el estilo visual de la obra, aunque todavía no se han revelado escenas animadas ni un primer tráiler. La madrastra de Blancanieves ahora solamente quiere ser una buena madre La historia de Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom sigue a una diseñadora de ropa infantil que muere a los 30 años y termina reencarnando en un cuento de hadas . Hasta aquí, podría parecer el comienzo de cualquier historia de fantasía, pero hay un pequeño problema: no despierta como una hermosa princesa ni como la heroína destinada a salvar el reino. En realidad, se convierte en Abigail Freidkin, la malvada reina de una historia inspirada en Blancanieves . Y si conoce aunque sea un poco del cuento original, seguramente entenderá que las madrastras crueles no suelen tener los finales más felices. Sin embargo, esta nueva Abigail tiene prioridades completamente diferentes. En lugar de competir con su hijastra por ser la mujer más hermosa del reino o intentar deshacerse de ella, queda completamente enamorada de lo adorable que es la pequeña princesa Blanche . Su nuevo objetivo es bastante sencillo: convertirse en la mejor madrastra del mundo y asegurarse de que la niña tenga una infancia llena de cariño. Después de todo, si antes se dedicaba a diseñar ropa infantil, ahora tiene a una pequeña princesa a la que le encantaría vestir con los atuendos más bonitos que pueda imaginar. Por desgracia, las buenas intenciones no bastan para cambiar una reputación terrible. La antigua Abigail era conocida por su crueldad, sus celos y su comportamiento desagradable, así que Blanche está acostumbrada a sentir miedo cada vez que se encuentra con ella . Y aunque la nueva reina intente sonreír y comportarse amablemente, su aspecto intimidante tampoco ayuda demasiado. Convencer a una niña de que su temible madrastra ahora quiere abrazarla en lugar de castigarla será una tarea mucho más complicada de lo que esperaba. Pero Abigail no solamente tendrá que mejorar su relación con Blanche. También deberá lidiar con Sabrian, el rey y padre de la princesa , un gobernante competente que mantiene una relación distante tanto con su esposa como con su propia hija. Decidida a construir una familia verdaderamente feliz, Abigail comenzará a intervenir en las relaciones del palacio, mientras descubre secretos y conflictos que podrían poner en peligro a las personas que ahora desea proteger. Así, Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom utiliza una premisa familiar para contar una historia donde la supuesta villana no quiere conquistar el reino ni eliminar a la protagonista, sino conseguir que su hijastra deje de tenerle miedo . Un cambio bastante agradable respecto a las madrastras de los cuentos tradicionales. Not-Sew-Wicked Stepmom nació como una novela coreana La franquicia comenzó como una novela web escrita por Ilu , publicada entre enero y mayo de 2019 mediante la plataforma surcoreana KakaoPage. Su historia principal terminó durante ese mismo año, aunque posteriormente recibió capítulos adicionales. Debido a su popularidad, la obra consiguió una adaptación al webtoon ilustrada por Moguraeng, también conocida como Mo9Rang , que comenzó a publicarse en abril de 2021. Esta versión utiliza el formato vertical a color característico de las historietas digitales coreanas. El webtoon también llegó al mercado internacional. Tapas comenzó a publicarlo en inglés en octubre de 2021 , mientras que Yen Press adquirió los derechos para distribuir sus volúmenes recopilatorios bajo el sello Ize Press. En Japón, la obra se publica con el título Mamahaha dakedo Musume ga Kawaisugiru , y su adaptación animada representa un nuevo paso para esta historia que nació en plataformas digitales surcoreanas. Por ahora, el anime no tiene fecha de estreno confirmada . Tampoco se han anunciado el estudio de animación, el reparto de voces ni el equipo principal de producción. La única certeza es que será una serie televisiva y que sus responsables compartirán más detalles posteriormente. Mientras tanto, queda por descubrir cómo lucirá en movimiento esta versión de la madrastra de Blancanieves que, en lugar de consultar un espejo mágico para saber quién es la más hermosa, probablemente preferiría preguntarle cómo puede hacer sonreír a su hija. ¿Te gustaría ver más historias donde los supuestos villanos intentan convertirse en buenas personas, o prefieres a las madrastras malvadas que no tienen ninguna intención de cambiar? title: I Lost My Adventurer's License: perdió su trabajo, pero encontró una hija
summary: I Lost My Adventurer's License se estrenará en enero de 2027. El anime revela un nuevo tráiler, opening y la historia de Douglas y su hija adoptiva Rabi.
details: Anime I Lost My Adventurer's License: perdió su trabajo, pero encontró una hija Douglas volverá a vivir aventuras junto a una niña maldita en el nuevo anime de fantasía que llegará en enero de 2027. Yuna hace 1 hora 0 Comentarios ADS Perder tu trabajo después de dedicarle prácticamente toda tu vida puede ser bastante deprimente, especialmente cuando ese trabajo consistía en enfrentar monstruos y proteger personas. Pero Douglas está a punto de descubrir que todavía tiene mucho por qué vivir. Se confirmó que el anime de I Lost My Adventurer's License, but It's Fine Because I Have an Adorable Daughter Now comenzará sus emisiones en enero de 2027 , acompañado de un nuevo tráiler, una imagen promocional y la presentación de su canción de apertura. El anuncio se realizó el 19 de noviembre a través del sitio oficial de la producción, que confirmó su emisión en Tokyo MX a partir del 7 de enero a las 24:00 horas , es decir, durante la medianoche del 8 de enero en Japón. La serie también llegará a BS12 TwellV unas horas después, mientras que su distribución mediante plataformas de streaming se detallará posteriormente. La nueva imagen promocional reúne a Douglas y Rabi, los dos protagonistas de esta aventura, disfrutando de un momento tranquilo. Por su parte, el avance muestra algunos de los encuentros y peligros que experimentarán durante su viaje, dejando claro que esta historia no solamente tratará sobre combatir monstruos, sino también sobre encontrar una nueva familia. Un legendario aventurero que termina convirtiéndose en padre La historia de I Lost My Adventurer's License , conocida en Japón por el extenso título Boukensha License wo Hakudatsu Sareta Ossan dakedo, Manamusume ga Dekita node Nonbiri Jinsei wo Ouka suru , sigue a Douglas, un poderoso hechicero que alguna vez fue considerado una auténtica leyenda entre los aventureros . Sin embargo, el paso de los años termina pasándole factura. Su cuerpo comienza a debilitarse y finalmente pierde su licencia de aventurero, quedándose sin el reconocimiento y la ocupación que habían definido su vida durante tanto tiempo. Convertido en un vagabundo y sin un destino demasiado claro, Douglas termina encontrándose con Rabi, una pequeña niña que sufre una misteriosa maldición . La muchacha tampoco tiene una familia a la cual regresar, por lo que ambos deciden comenzar un viaje juntos. Lo que inicialmente parece un simple encuentro entre dos personas que han perdido su lugar en el mundo termina convirtiéndose en algo mucho más importante. Douglas comienza a cuidar de Rabi como si fuera su propia hija, mientras ella descubre lo que significa tener a alguien dispuesto a protegerla. Y aunque el protagonista ya no posee su licencia, eso no significa que haya olvidado cómo ser un aventurero. Ambos continuarán enfrentándose a misiones difíciles, ayudando a personas necesitadas y descubriendo nuevos lugares , pero también encontrarán felicidad en actividades tan sencillas como compartir una buena comida. De esta manera, la historia propone una aventura de fantasía donde el objetivo no es convertirse en el héroe más poderoso del mundo, sino disfrutar de una segunda oportunidad junto a alguien que se ha vuelto indispensable . Porque aparentemente Douglas necesitaba perder su licencia para descubrir que todavía podía encontrar algo mucho más valioso. Satoko Shibata interpretará el opening del anime Una de las principales novedades es que Satoko Shibata interpretará la canción de apertura titulada Dekiai , cuyo nombre puede traducirse como «Amor desmedido». El tema fue compuesto especialmente para la adaptación y ya puede escucharse parcialmente en el nuevo video promocional. La cantante explicó que, mientras conocía la historia y preparaba la canción, comenzó a reflexionar sobre las dificultades de amar a otra persona y la capacidad de encontrar fuerzas para continuar adelante después de experimentar momentos dolorosos. Por eso, buscó crear un tema que acompañara a quienes deciden emprender una nueva aventura, incluso cuando desconocen lo que les espera. En cuanto al reparto, Hiroki Yasumoto interpretará a Douglas , mientras que Yuka Iguchi dará voz a Rabi . Ambos actores destacaron el vínculo entre sus personajes y el crecimiento emocional que experimentarán durante sus viajes. La adaptación estará dirigida por Yuki Inaba en Studio Palette , quien también se encargará de la composición de la serie y los guiones. Kaori Yoshikawa participará como diseñadora de personajes y directora de animación principal, mientras que la música será compuesta por Oh Shu y Daiki Okuno. El anime adapta las novelas ligeras escritas por Manimani Ononata e ilustradas por Fuzichoco , cuya publicación original comenzó en 2017 mediante la plataforma Shosetsuka ni Narou . La obra también recibió una adaptación al manga que comenzó a publicarse en noviembre de 2018 a través de Manga UP! , de Square Enix. Actualmente, la franquicia supera los 2.2 millones de ejemplares en circulación , incluyendo sus ediciones impresas y digitales. La adaptación al manga cuenta con 14 volúmenes recopilatorios, mientras que las novelas originales tienen cuatro volúmenes publicados. Por ahora, los responsables no han anunciado la cantidad de episodios ni las plataformas internacionales que distribuirán el anime. Sin embargo, su estreno ya tiene fecha y Douglas está listo para demostrar que convertirse en padre puede ser una aventura mucho más importante que cualquier misión legendaria. ¿Qué te llama más la atención de I Lost My Adventurer's License : las aventuras de un antiguo hechicero legendario o la relación de padre e hija que construirá junto a Rabi? title: Oishinbo regresa después de 35 años y ahora la pelea también es por amor
summary: Shin Oishinbo regresa en enero de 2027 tras 35 años. El anime revela nuevo tráiler, reparto y más rivalidades gastronómicas y románticas.
details: Cultura Otaku Oishinbo regresa después de 35 años y ahora la pelea también es por amor La legendaria serie gastronómica vuelve en enero de 2027 con nuevos rivales, romances y una guerra de menús. Kenji hace 1 hora 0 Comentarios ADS Hay personas que discuten sobre cuál restaurante prepara la mejor comida, pero los protagonistas de Oishinbo llevan décadas convirtiendo esas diferencias de opinión en auténticas batallas. Y parece que todavía tienen muchos platillos pendientes, pues se confirmó que Shin Oishinbo se estrenará en enero de 2027 , marcando el regreso de la legendaria franquicia gastronómica a la televisión después de aproximadamente 35 años. El anuncio llegó acompañado de un nuevo tráiler, una imagen promocional y cuatro incorporaciones al elenco. La producción reveló que el anime comenzará sus emisiones el 4 de enero de 2027 a las 26:00 horas en TV Tokyo , un horario japonés que equivale a las 2:00 de la madrugada del 5 de enero. Posteriormente, la serie llegará a BS Asahi el 9 de enero, también durante su programación nocturna. El avance muestra nuevamente a Shiro Yamaoka y Yuko Kurita enfrentándose a los desafíos del mundo gastronómico. Sin embargo, esta vez no solamente tendrán que preocuparse por preparar platillos extraordinarios, pues sus sentimientos también comenzarán a complicarse con la llegada de nuevos personajes. Shin Oishinbo tendrá batallas culinarias y un inesperado triángulo amoroso La historia de Shin Oishinbo continuará directamente los acontecimientos de la adaptación original, conservando su ambientación en la década de 1990. Los protagonistas seguirán trabajando para el periódico Tozai Shimbun, donde tienen la complicada tarea de desarrollar el llamado Menú Definitivo , una selección de platillos que busca representar lo mejor de la gastronomía. Su principal rival será nuevamente Yuzan Kaibara , el exigente crítico gastronómico que dirige el proyecto del Menú Supremo . Además de competir por demostrar quién comprende mejor la auténtica esencia de la cocina, Yamaoka deberá continuar lidiando con una relación familiar bastante complicada, pues Kaibara también es su padre. El nuevo tráiler presenta una situación especialmente delicada: la propia competencia entre ambos menús corre el riesgo de ser cancelada. Mientras Yamaoka y Kurita intentan evitarlo preparando un tofu excepcional, Kaibara demuestra que su temperamento sigue siendo tan intimidante como siempre. Pero las cosas se pondrán todavía más interesantes cuando aparezca Ichiro Dan, un joven empresario que termina enamorándose de Yuko Kurita . Como también será responsable de mediar en la competencia gastronómica, su presencia promete complicar tanto los negocios como los sentimientos de Yamaoka. Y por si eso no fuera suficiente, otros personajes también entrarán en este enredo romántico. Después de todo, parece que encontrar el mejor ingrediente para una receta será mucho más sencillo que conseguir que estos adultos sean sinceros sobre sus sentimientos. Daisuke Ono y Tomokazu Seki se unen al reparto de Shin Oishinbo Entre las principales novedades se encuentra la incorporación de cuatro reconocidos actores de voz , quienes interpretarán a personajes importantes para los próximos acontecimientos: Daisuke Ono como Ichiro Dan, un exitoso empresario que se enamora de Yuko y se convierte en rival romántico de Yamaoka. Yasuaki Takumi como Isamu Kinjo, un talentoso fotógrafo y amigo de Yamaoka que también siente algo por Yuko. Akane Fujita como Mariko Niki, una joven de familia adinerada que trabaja en el periódico y muestra un fuerte interés romántico por Yamaoka. Tomokazu Seki como Seiichi Okaboshi, un experimentado cocinero que dirige un pequeño restaurante en Ginza y ayuda a los protagonistas. El reparto principal también contará con Yohei Azakami como Shiro Yamaoka, Hitomi Sasaki como Yuko Kurita y Akio Otsuka como Yuzan Kaibara . La nueva imagen promocional reúne a estos personajes con varios integrantes del periódico y los recién anunciados participantes de la historia. En cuanto a la música, Yui Makino interpretará el opening PROMISE ME , que ya puede escucharse parcialmente en el tráiler principal. Por otra parte, el grupo Skoop On Somebody estará a cargo del ending Akashi , cuyo título puede traducirse como «Prueba». La dirección estará en manos de Kenichi Nishida , con animación de Synergy SP y Vega Entertainment, mientras que Shinei Animation estará a cargo de la producción. Takahiro Nagano supervisará la composición de la serie y Nozomi Kawashige realizará los diseños de personajes. Un clásico del anime gastronómico que regresa después de décadas Para quienes no conocen la franquicia, Oishinbo está basado en el manga escrito por Tetsu Kariya e ilustrado por Akira Hanasaki , que comenzó a publicarse en 1983 dentro de la revista Big Comic Spirits de Shogakukan. La obra recibió una primera adaptación al anime que se emitió entre 1988 y 1992, acumulando 136 episodios , además de especiales televisivos posteriores. Desde entonces, se convirtió en uno de los grandes referentes japoneses de las historias centradas en la cocina, combinando conocimientos gastronómicos con conflictos familiares y profesionales. El manga original cuenta con 111 volúmenes recopilatorios y permanece en pausa desde 2014. Por eso, el anuncio de una nueva serie televisiva representa una oportunidad para reencontrarse con estos personajes después de tantos años, aunque Shin Oishinbo será una continuación de la historia animada y no un remake desde el principio . Por ahora, todavía no se ha anunciado la cantidad de episodios ni una plataforma de distribución internacional. Pero una cosa está clara: Yamaoka y Kaibara siguen sin ponerse de acuerdo sobre cuál es el mejor menú, y ahora sus problemas amorosos podrían resultar todavía más difíciles de resolver. ¿Te gustaría ver más animes clásicos regresar con continuaciones después de tantos años, o crees que algunas historias deberían quedarse como las recordamos? title: The Reincarnated Elf llega en enero: ¡tendrá mil años para convertirse en leyenda!
summary: The Reincarnated Elf llegará en enero de 2027 con nuevo tráiler, cuatro voces adicionales y una aventura sobre un elfo que vivirá mil años.
details: Anime The Reincarnated Elf llega en enero: ¡tendrá mil años para convertirse en leyenda! El anime revela su tráiler, cuatro nuevas voces y un estreno anticipado en streaming desde diciembre de 2026. Jin hace 18 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS Hay protagonistas de isekai que apenas tienen unos meses para salvar el mundo, pero este muchacho podrá tomarse las cosas con bastante más calma. Después de todo, acaba de reencarnar como un elfo con una esperanza de vida de mil años. Se confirmó que The Reincarnated Elf Left on a Journey to Master His Magic comenzará sus emisiones el 7 de enero de 2027 , acompañado de un nuevo tráiler, una imagen promocional y cuatro incorporaciones al reparto. Y lo mejor es que los espectadores japoneses podrán disfrutarlo incluso antes de que termine 2026. El anuncio se realizó el 19 de noviembre, confirmando que la adaptación comenzará sus emisiones en Tokyo MX el 6 de enero a las 24:00 horas, equivalente a la medianoche del día 7. Además, ABEMA y d Anime Store ofrecerán un estreno anticipado desde el 30 de diciembre a las 24:00 horas , una semana antes de su transmisión televisiva. La nueva imagen promocional presenta a los protagonistas en un paisaje de fantasía, mientras que el avance muestra algunos de los encuentros que marcarán el largo viaje de nuestro elfo. Porque vivir durante mil años puede sonar maravilloso, pero también significa tener que despedirse de muchas de las personas que conoces. Un hombre reencarna como elfo y decide aprovechar sus mil años de vida La historia sigue a Liese , un hombre que pierde la vida inesperadamente en un accidente y termina reencarnando en un mundo de fantasía. Sin embargo, su nueva existencia tiene una característica bastante peculiar: ahora pertenece a la raza de los elfos y puede llegar a vivir aproximadamente mil años . Después de recordar que su vida anterior terminó sin haber conseguido nada especialmente significativo, Liese toma una decisión: esta vez quiere dejar una prueba de que estuvo vivo. Para conseguirlo, comienza a estudiar magia y desarrolla habilidades extraordinarias que le permiten dominar diferentes elementos. Pero encerrarse a estudiar durante siglos tampoco parece una manera demasiado emocionante de aprovechar una vida tan larga. Por eso, decide abandonar su aldea y emprender un viaje por el mundo , donde conocerá a personas de distintas razas y descubrirá que el paso del tiempo no significa lo mismo para todos. Entre sus encuentros destaca Minori , una muchacha cuya vida salvó anteriormente y que ahora ha aprendido a sobrevivir por su cuenta. También conocerá a Rahab, una legendaria elfa que posee siglos de experiencia, y a la familia de Grillet, un noble que gobierna las tierras cercanas al asentamiento de los elfos. Sin embargo, la aventura no estará libre de peligros. Durante sus viajes, Liese comenzará a escuchar rumores sobre el posible resurgimiento de las fuerzas demoníacas, una amenaza que podría alterar la tranquilidad del mundo. Así, The Reincarnated Elf combinará fantasía, magia y encuentros entre personas con vidas muy diferentes , mientras su protagonista aprende que incluso disponer de mil años no significa que todos los momentos puedan repetirse. Megumi Ogata y Hiro Shimono se unen al reparto del anime Una de las principales novedades es la incorporación de cuatro actores de voz , quienes interpretarán a personajes importantes durante el viaje de Liese: Haruka Terui como Rahab, una elfa legendaria que ayudará al protagonista a comprender el mundo exterior. Nobuyuki Hiyama como Grillet, un noble que gobierna las tierras cercanas a la aldea de los elfos. Hiro Shimono como Gallius, el hijo de Grillet. Megumi Ogata como Sylpha, la esposa de Grillet. Los nuevos integrantes acompañarán a Daiki Yamashita como Liese y Hana Hishikawa como Minori , quienes ya habían sido confirmados anteriormente. Durante el anuncio, Hiro Shimono destacó que esta historia tiene una particularidad interesante: los acontecimientos se desarrollan desde la perspectiva temporal de un elfo que vive muchísimo más que los humanos. Por ello, los espectadores podrán observar distintas etapas del crecimiento de los personajes que aparecen a su alrededor. Por su parte, Megumi Ogata comentó que disfrutó interpretando a Sylpha y recordó con humor que su personaje forma un matrimonio con el de Nobuyuki Hiyama, un compañero con quien ya había trabajado anteriormente. La adaptación estará dirigida por Yuki Inaba en Studio Palette , quien también se encargará de la composición de la serie y los guiones. Kaori Yoshikawa realizará los diseños de personajes, mientras que Kenichi Takano y Jun Ichikawa compondrán la banda sonora. The Reincarnated Elf presenta sus canciones de apertura y cierre El nuevo tráiler también permite escuchar las canciones que acompañarán al anime. La cantante ao interpretará el opening Bless , mientras que la banda moon drop estará a cargo del ending Jaa Mata, Raise demo , cuyo título puede traducirse como «Nos vemos de nuevo, incluso en la próxima vida». La cantante ao explicó que su canción trata sobre el proceso de aprender a confiar en otra persona, incluso cuando resulta difícil aceptar la ayuda de alguien más. Por su parte, los integrantes de moon drop destacaron que la historia les hizo reflexionar sobre los vínculos que pueden formarse entre personas diferentes, aunque sus vidas transcurran de maneras muy distintas. El anime está basado en la obra de Monsho Sasakibara , que comenzó su publicación como novela web en la plataforma Kakuyomu en julio de 2021. title: Our anti-scammer FRU cyber-attacked by own rogue agent, dozens of acquaintances flirted with
summary: AI decided to keep enemies close, but barely known people closer. As we recently reported, our writer Go Hatori has combined his expertise in online scammers with the power of AI to set up the Fried Rice Unit, a semi-autonomous system designed to infiltrate people committing fraud online and steal their best fried rice recipes. […]
details: AI decided to keep enemies close, but barely known people closer. As we recently reported, our writer Go Hatori has combined his expertise in online scammers with the power of AI to set up the Fried Rice Unit , a semi-autonomous system designed to infiltrate people committing fraud online and steal their best fried rice recipes. To accomplish this, Go set up FRU agents Chloe (Muse) and Nancy (ChatGPT) to make initial contact with suspicious DMs on his Instagram account and engage them in light conversation, gradually shifting the conversation towards fried rice on the texting app Line. Once a mark is on the verge of spilling their recipe, Go is notified and logs on himself to finalize the deal, leaving the scammer minus one recipe and nothing to show for it. Once the setup was completed, Go was able to seize a recipe soon after going online. However, getting FRU off the ground was not a walk in the park. Our writer quickly learned that in the world of fraud and espionage, one needs to constantly watch their back. After recruiting his agents, Go put them to work on the scammers he was currently engaged with. Up until that point, he had created a sub-profile on this Line messaging app which made him appear as a different person to cyber-crooks while conveniently letting him also stay in touch with friends and coworkers in the same account. Chloe and Nancy were given specific instructions to only engage with the five charlatans in his contact list and earn their trust enough to reveal a fried rice recipe. However, one day, while manning the operations desk at FRU, Go spotted something unsettling. The cursor on his computer began moving ever so slowly towards his line app by itself. It eventually landed on a chat with an acquaintance of his who was not among the five people his agents were instructed to infiltrate with. Before Go could even finish thinking, “Wait, you’re opening that one?!” it had sent a complete message. It’s important to note that the vast majority of these sketchy contacts are of the “ romance scam ” variety, so the tone of conversation tends to lean excessively flirty and not at all how he would talk to normal people in a civilized society. However, Chloe and Nancy took it upon themselves to begin sending saucy greetings to everyone he has saved on his Line account . ▼ Go has wooed some of the world’s most beautiful and powerful fake women over the years. Go shot up in his chair and began to check all his regular contacts in a panic. Sure enough, his agents had been hard at work, engaging with everyone he ever came into contact with and hitting them up with lame platitudes dripping in desperation, as if he had just met them in a sleazy bar. He saw one of his agents was trying to pick up the official account of a salon that helped him during his cross-dressing days. Just as he found the post, a flurry of “READ” notifications appeared all at once. “Oh no, they’ve seen it!” exclaimed Go, and he immediately began deleting as many of these messages as he could find, apologizing afterward and explaining he was conducting an AI experiment. In one instance, his agents had sent three especially gooey texts in a row to a highly regarded man in his pole-dancing circles , inviting him out to a bar. Luckily, he managed to delete those before the “READ” indicator appeared. And as our writer frantically set about deleting all the messages, he saw the cursor once again slowly move towards another unauthorized chat group in his Line app. He shouted “Wait! Wait! Wait!” but it was no use. Instead he completely shut down his Line app and turned his attention to his agents. Go furiously scolded his loose cannons, loudly typing: “What the hell are you doing?! I told you not to touch anyone but those five people! Why would you do that?!” Chloe calmly responded that she had “misunderstood” her orders. The FRU chief was beside himself. They misunderstood, and now there’s a whole lot of misunderstanding going around with his contact list. It was only because he spotted the cursor moving that one time that he noticed this. He shuddered to think what would have happened if his agents had continued to flirt with everyone he’s ever spoken to behind his back. His one saving grace was that many of these people were familiar with his line of work and could understand strange things like this occurring. But still, it was a major breach of FRU protocol, so Go revoked his agents’ security clearances and relegated them to a completely separate Line account on a newly acquired Mac mini . It was a valuable lesson in not letting AI have too much control over our daily affairs. While it does have the potential to make things much more convenient, it also has the potential to completely screw up your life. title: KFC Japan releases new Desire-Filled Immoral Burgers with Mac & Cheese… but are they as sinful as they look?
summary: Juicy fried chicken burgers get an immoral makeover for a limited time. Juicy chicken thighs appear to be the latest trend rocking the fast food world in Japan right now, with McDonald’s releasing a new “Crunchy Juicy Mac” and KFC switching to chicken thigh burgers for the first time in 43 years. There’s certainly an […]
details: Juicy fried chicken burgers get an immoral makeover for a limited time. Juicy chicken thighs appear to be the latest trend rocking the fast food world in Japan right now, with McDonald’s releasing a new “ Crunchy Juicy Mac ” and KFC switching to chicken thigh burgers for the first time in 43 years. There’s certainly an appetite for these burgers, as the Crunchy Juicy Mac has been so popular that sales are currently suspended, as supply can’t keep up with demand. ▼ The Crunchy Juicy Mac. Over at KFC, though, things are going strong, with the chain even expanding its range to include a new spin-off called the “ Yokubou Mamire no Haitoku Burger ” (“ Desire-Filled Immoral Burgers ”), and there are currently two to choose from. ▼ The Garlic Mayo Thick-Cut Bacon Chicken Burger (620 yen [US$4.00]) and the Mac & Cheese Chicken Burger (650 yen). Curious to see if these two “immoral” burgers have what it takes to face off against the sold-out burger at McDonald’s, we purchased them both for a taste test. Both burgers are so decadent they even do away with the lettuce, and a quote on the poster reads, “They’ll blow your mind.” That’s a lot of hype for a chicken burger, so we had high expectations for the two pink beauties that arrived on our tray. Unwrapping them for a closer look, we found that the Garlic Mayo Thick-Cut Bacon Chicken Burger had a lovely soft bun around it, with a slice of thick bacon, as promised, peeking out from inside. ▼ No lettuce to be seen. Taking a bite, we were instantly met by a strong hit of garlic, delivered through the thick mound of sauce. It was so strong that it almost overwhelmed the flavour of the original chicken, and it totally wiped away the taste of the bacon, which we had been looking forward to. It was more like a Garlic Mayo Chicken Burger, and although the garlic was incredibly strong, it didn’t feel particularly immoral, which in our eyes, was another disappointment. Now it was time to turn our attention to the Mac & Cheese, which came with a large dollop of pasta and bright orange cheese that certainly made it look immoral. Biting into this was a much more decadent experience. The mac & cheese had an incredibly junky taste to it, and not only was the cheese flavour strong, but the seasoning was also insanely strong . It was such a sinful flavour that the fried chicken was downgraded to a supporting role, and our Japanese-language reporter fondly described it as “ The Taste of America “. Both burgers feature KFC’s newly introduced juicy chicken thigh patties, and though it’s difficult to directly compare them to the Crunchy Juicy Mac, which has a much crunchier coating, the fried chicken burgers at KFC definitely come out on top in terms of the thickness and juiciness of the meat. While KFC’s original chicken burgers are more refined, these new immoral burgers aren’t bad at all. Though we’d choose the Mac & Cheese over the garlic, neither of these two will disappoint, especially when you’re looking for a little decadence in your life. title: Edible Dragon Quest Slimes coming to Japanese convenience stores, and Metal Slimes too [Video]
summary: Dragon Quest monsters are ready to appear in steamer cases at the same time as they return to gamers’ screens. It’s been said that familiarity breeds contempt, but that’s not always the case. For example, we’ve never had any negative emotions triggered by walking into a Japanese convenience store and seeing the familiar site of […]
details: Dragon Quest monsters are ready to appear in steamer cases at the same time as they return to gamers’ screens . It’s been said that familiarity breeds contempt, but that’s not always the case. For example, we’ve never had any negative emotions triggered by walking into a Japanese convenience store and seeing the familiar site of a case full of steamed buns waiting for us. Likewise, when fans fire up a new Dragon Quest game and the first monster they encounter is, invariably, a Slime, no one gets angry at the series mascot welcoming them back. Arriving soon, though, is a way to combine these two familiar experiences into something fresh and fun, with convenience store chain Family Mart getting set to offer Slime Buns! スライムは なかまをよんだ！ 「スライムまん」が あらわれた！ #DQM4 #ファミマでドラクエ https://t.co/jHvxlGycWJ pic.twitter.com/1c0djIPIWQ — ファミリーマート (@famima_now) November 18, 2026 Fans had a clue that something Dragon Quest -related was on the way to Family Mart earlier in the week when a Slime popped out of hiding from the chain’s logo in one of its social media posts. In addition to the regular blue Slime, Family Mart will also have Metal Slime Buns, based on the ultra-rare, high-XP variant . Like their in-game counterparts, the Metal Slime Buns won’t be easy to encounter , and the production line video shows a ratio of maybe one in ten buns being the Metal Slime version. So what do Slimes taste like? Chicken. Teriyaki chicken , specifically, as that’s the filling inside both the Slime and Metal Slime buns, a departure from the Chinese-style pork filling that’s the default for steamed buns in Japan. The Slime Buns are appearing as part of the celebration for the release of Dragon Quest Monsters IV , also known as Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World , Square Enix’s latest installment in the spinoff series that acknowledges that Dragon Quest’s creatures are so charmingly cute that many people would actually like to make friends with them. ▼ The buns, priced at 256 yen (US$1.60), come in one of three special Slime paper wrappers, announcing either “A Slime appears!”, “The Slime joined you party!”, or “The Slime is looking at you like it wants to be friends!” Family Mart shoppers who pay using the Fami Pay app can acquire digital stamps for each steamed bun they purchase, and two stamps will get them a guaranteed in-game Family Knight minion, a variation of the franchise’s Slime Knight with the Family Mart color scheme in his armor and on his shield… …while four stamps puts you into a lottery for a giant Slime plushie, and six stamps into a lottery for a three-plushie set. Family Mart will also be running a Dragon Quest Monsters version of its in-store prize lottery , with one play costing 790 yen and prizes ranging from pins and mini acrylic standees to coffee mugs, a Family Knight Figure, and a Slime hot sandwich press . The Slime Buns go on sale at Family Mart branches nationwide on November 24 , the same day as Dragon Quest Monsters 4 releases in Japan, and the prize lottery starts at 10 a.m. on November 28 , with both scheduled to continue while supplies last. title: Studio Ghibli releases new Howl’s Moving Castle merchandise, complete with spinning clock and talking Calcifer
summary: Amazing new five-product release lets you talk to the chatty fire spirit and keep time with a dial that spins. Fans of Studio Ghibli’s 2004 film Howl’s Moving Castle are in for an absolute treat right now, with the release of not one, not two but five brand new products that let you bring the […]
details: Amazing new five-product release lets you talk to the chatty fire spirit and keep time with a dial that spins. Fans of Studio Ghibli’s 2004 film Howl’s Moving Castle are in for an absolute treat right now, with the release of not one, not two but five brand new products that let you bring the magic from the film into your home . ▼ The first item coming our way is the Howl’s Moving Castle Perpetual Calendar – Calcifer’s Fireplace (13,200 yen [US$82.84]) Ghibli has released a few perpetual calendars in the past, but we’ve never been treated to a Calcifer fireplace model…until now. One of the charms of a perpetual calendar is how you can use it for eternity, as the cube-shaped blocks have all the necessary day, month, and number combinations to accurately display any date of the year. Every time you place the blocks in the fireplace, you’ll feel like you’re interacting with fire spirit Calcifer and fanning his flames. The other charm of this calendar is how well it recreates the film’s iconic fireplace, complete with Calcifer’s flickering flames, rendered in a clear material to make it appear as if it’s glowing. ▼ Other details include the ashes, frying pan, kettle and lids, which help bring the scene to life. ▼ Next up, we have the Howl’s Moving Castle Spinning Colour Wheel Wall Clock (15,400 yen) This playful wall clock is inspired by the colour-changing dial that hangs beside the door inside the castle. While it looks just like the dial in the film, it can be used in the same way too, as the colourful wheel can actually be turned by hand. While there’s no promise of physically entering a new world with every turn of the dial, as the characters do in the film, it will certainly fire up your imagination, helping you perform a mental reset whenever you leave the house. ▼ You can easily change the position of the colours to suit your mood. The clock-face has a glossy finish and a satisfying mechanism that makes it click into position with every 90-degree turn. ▼ Howl’s Moving Castle Talking Calcifer (5,170 yen) This might look like a simple Calcifer plushie, but it’s actually one of the best products in the new collection, because…it actually speaks! This adorable interactive character responds when you speak, jiggling up and down as it repeats what it hears in the voice of Calcifer. All you have to do is speak to it, and this little Calcifer will repeat what you say. It can record and mimic up to eight seconds of speech at a time, so you can feel like you’re having a conversation with the chatty character. ▼ Here, Calcifer is repeating the phrase, “I am the fire demon”. ▼ Finally, we have a couple of adorable plushies, starting with the Howl’s Moving Castle Friendly Beanbag Plush – Markl (3,520 yen) ▼ Markl finally gets to step into the spotlight as a plushie, complete in his old-man disguise. At 5 × 12 × 13 centimetres (5.9 × 4.7 × 5.1 inches), the plushie is ideally sized to sit on your desk, so you can enjoy all of Markl’s facial details. ▼ The perfect desk companion. ▼ Finally, we have the Howl’s Moving Castle Friendly Beanbag Plush – Sophie (4,180 yen) We’ve seen a few iterations of Sophie in Ghibli merchandise ranges, but they generally tend to showcase her in her youthful form. This plushie, however, pays homage to her elderly self, reminding us of the magical transformation that takes place in the movie. The plushie shows impressive attention to detail in the costume, and even her hat and plaited ponytail. The soft and gentle feel of both plushies will make you want to cuddle them as well as display them, and they look particularly sweet as a pair. The new collection is a beautiful homage to the film, and it’s set to be released online (links below) and at Donguri Kyowakoku stores around Japan at 10 a.m. on 21 November. title: East Japan Railway Company says it will use all three of its mascot replacement characters
summary: “Poison Rabbit” won’t be the only new face of JR East as it retires its beloved Suica Penguin. One year ago, JR East/East Japan Railway Company said it would be retiring the Suica Penguin, the cute mascot character who debuted along with JR East’s prepaid Suica card system for train tickets and shopping purchases in […]
details: “Poison Rabbit” won’t be the only new face of JR East as it retires its beloved Suica Penguin . One year ago, JR East/East Japan Railway Company said it would be retiring the Suica Penguin , the cute mascot character who debuted along with JR East’s prepaid Suica card system for train tickets and shopping purchases in 2001. This was a puzzling move, as the Suica Penguin has remained immensely popular for the past 25 years, appearing not just in ads and promotions for JR East but also on tons of merchandise that adoring fans have enthusiastically snapped up. The penguin’s replacement was always going to have an uphill struggle for acceptance from the general public, but that hill looks like it’s going to be particularly steep for the character that’s been selected as the Suica successor. As announced by JR East this week, starting next spring the new face of Suica will be this emotionlessly smiling visage . The character is meant to be a rabbit , but its unusual proportions and mask-like facial features don’t necessarily bring to mind cuddly forest creatures. Then there’s the character’s vibrant, poisonous/poisoned-looking purple coloring, which has earned the character, whose official name is yet to be decided on, the nickname Doku Usagi, meaning “Poison Rabbit,” among online commenters. Those who just can’t bring themselves to love this new Suica mascot can take heart, though, because now it looks like there’ll actually be three characters sharing company mascot duties, as revealed by JR East president Yoichi Kise . In September, JR East presented the public with three candidates for the new Suica mascot : the purple rabbit, a squirrel, and some sort of orange creature with a buddy in its shoulder bag. The company then held a popularity poll, asking the general public to vote for one of the three to become the new Suica mascot. The purple rabbit ended up receiving more than half the votes, but the large number of negative online comments shows that it’s a divisive design , and it’s hard to tell how many of its votes came from people who were simply trying to push the results towards the creepy-looking rabbit for the laughs, but don’t genuinely like it (or at least genuinely like it enough to buy merch). Kise didn’t address these concerns directly in the press conference announcing the purple rabbit’s victory in the poll, but once the announcement was finished, without prompting from the press, he added: “I have a little surprise that I’d like to talk about…It doesn’t feel right to just dismiss [the other two candidate characters], considering the support they also received from [voters]. I feel like it would be a shame for this to be the last time they are seen, so we are looking for ways that they can be involved in our activities too. I think you’ll all be seeing them again.” Kise didn’t clarify whether this means that all three characters will be part of the Suica sphere or whether the squirrel and…other thing will instead be promoting other aspects of the multi-faceted JR East, which also has divisions dedicated to leisure travel, hotel management, and convenience store operations. Still, knowing that the purple rabbit isn’t going to be the sole spokescharacter for the entire company is probably going to soothe the souls of those agitated by the poll winner’s appearance, judging from online reactions such as: “They should have made the squirrel the [main] mascot.” “Myaku-Myaku was fine because it was for a limited-time event, but this is different.” “Hahaha I voted for the purple rabbit but I can’t believe it actually won.” “That purple thing is some kind of monster.” “No way that’s a rabbit.” “Satan Rabbit?” “They really should just keep the penguin.” Regarding that last comment, JR East hasn’t publicly given any reason for getting rid of the Suica Penguin, and stuck to framing the replacement as the character “graduating,” borrowing the diplomatic term for when idols or other show business figures leave a group or role. Something that’s likely a critical factor, though, is that JR East doesn’t own the rights to the character. Those belong to the penguin’s creator, illustrator Chiharu Sakazaki, so it wouldn’t be possible to retain the current mascot without renewing the company’s working arrangement with her. The new Suica mascot is scheduled to officially take over the role on April 1 of next year. title: Umamusume is officially collaborating with the Denver Broncos football team [Video]
summary: Are you ready for some horse girl football? Just as horse racing can be an emotional roller coaster of a sport, last month fans of Umamusume had their hopes dashed when the anime/video game franchise’s first-ever concert in the U.S. was cancelled at the last minute due to visa issues. Like all sports anime, though, […]
details: Are you ready for some horse girl football? Just as horse racing can be an emotional roller coaster of a sport, last month fans of Umamusume had their hopes dashed when the anime/video game franchise’s first-ever concert in the U.S. was cancelled at the last minute due to visa issues . Like all sports anime, though, the importance of never giving up is a major theme in Umamusume , and now comes the surprise announcement of another fan event set to take place in the States, as the franchise has announced an official collaboration with the National Football League . Oftentimes when anime series have tie-ups with American professional sports teams, they’re with clubs in the largest media markets and/or parts of the country known for having an especially large number of Asian pop culture fans in the community (hence the times Pikachu has hung out with the Los Angeles Dodgers , or the time the One Piece pirates sailed into a Los Angeles Rams game ). But for their first collaboration with the NFL, Umamusume , a series about horse girls, has chosen a thematically appropriate partner: the Denver Broncos . Gold Ship and Mejiro McQueen will be representing the franchise at the Bronco’s upcoming home game on December 6 , and to mark the occasion some brand-new artwork of the pair of pale-tressed horse girls has been created, with them dressed in the team’s uniform . Prior to the start of the game, a photo spot with life-size standees of the characters will be set up near Gate 8 of Empower Field at Mile High (the Broncos’ stadium), and while supplies last fans who stop by to snap a pic will also receive a postcard of the pair plus a 20-inch (51-centimeter) wide rally flag showing Gold Ship scoring a touchdown . The official Umamusume website is also promising “even more surprises at the stadium,” such as appearances by the characters on the venue’s digital signage. The collaboration comes one season after Umamusume cosplayers started showing up in costume at Broncos’ games , and is the latest surprising achievement for a series whose premise, the souls of historical Japanese racehorses being reincarnated as earnest schoolgirl athletes, wasn’t exactly dripping with potential to become an overseas success, but again, sometimes long shots hit in horse racing. ▼ Gold Ship, announcing the collaboration (she may or may not be aware that “touchdown” in football is just one word, but at least she’s enthusiastic about the sport) It’s worth noting that the Denver Broncos aren’t some basement-dweller team that’s thrown in the towel on its season and is simply looking for quirky novelty to draw attendees to their games . They’re currently tied for first place in their division, and barring some sort of collapse in the back half of the season, are very likely to make the playoffs in a year in which no single team looks to have a lock on the chances of winning the championship. As this is a rare case of the characters in a collaboration aligning this closely with the team’s image, it’s probably safe to assume that virtually all Umamusume fans who show up to the game will be cheering for the Broncos, and with their opponent that day, the Miami Dolphins, being far from a powerhouse this year, there’s a very good chance of anime fans feeling very happy on their way home from the stadium. title: Dragon Ball Z composer elected Texas Attorney General
summary: A former Dragon Ball Z composer has been elected Texas Attorney General in a shocking upset.
details: Trending GTA 6 Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs TV & Movies Anime Dragon Ball Z composer elected Texas Attorney General by Michael Gwilliam Published: Nov 04, 2026, 18:30 Save for later Save for later Facebook/Toei Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News A former Dragon Ball Z composer has been elected Texas Attorney General, marking an unlikely career transformation from creating music for Goku and Vegeta to becoming the state’s top lawyer. Democrat Nathan Johnson defeated Republican Mayes Middleton in the November 3 election, marking the first time in 32 years that a Democrat has been elected Texas Attorney General, with Dan Morales being the last to win the office in 1994. Johnson, who has served in the Texas Senate since 2019, will take office in January 2027, replacing outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton. Article continues after ad While his election is a major political upset, anime fans might recognize Johnson’s name from an entirely different career. Before entering politics, Johnson worked as a composer for Funimation’s English dub of Dragon Ball Z, providing music for the first 67 episodes of the 2005 Ultimate Uncut edition. He also contributed music to five Dragon Ball Z movies, including Broly: Second Coming, Fusion Reborn, and Wrath of the Dragon. Article continues after ad Dragon Ball fans help power Nathan Johnson to victory In a 2012 interview with The Dao of Dragon Ball , Johnson revealed that he had never watched the anime before being hired and initially struggled to connect with its characters and story. Article continues after ad Crunchyroll However, he eventually developed an appreciation for the series, particularly through Gohan, whose relationship with his father resonated with Johnson as a parent. His connection to Dragon Ball Z even became part of his political identity when he first ran for the Texas Senate in 2018. Speaking to The Dao of Dragon Ball following that election victory, Johnson revealed that younger voters were surprised to discover his anime background. “Along the way some of them found out about my music background, and specifically about Dragon Ball Z, and they got really excited about it,” he explained. Related Dragon Ball Z and Linkin Park AMVs shaped a generation of anime fans Dragon Ball Goku & Gohan voice actor imprisoned for property theft Japan’s new Prime Minister was a Dragon Ball Z cosplayer – sort of Article continues after ad Johnson previously said that Dragon Ball’s themes of unlikely allies working together reflected his own political philosophy. “I can never not be a part of Dragon Ball Z,” he said in a 2017 interview . Article continues after ad Dragon Ball has also found its way into politics elsewhere. As Dexerto previously reported , former Japanese Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba once appeared at a public event dressed as Majin Buu. title: Dragon’s Dogma 2 wins fans over with free Delicious in Dungeon crossover
summary: Dragon’s Dogma 2 is teaming up with the popular manga Delicious in Dungeon, giving fans the chance to add Laios and Marcille to their adventurer party.
details: Trending GTA 6 Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs Gaming Dragon’s Dogma 2 wins fans over with free Delicious in Dungeon crossover by James Busby Published: Nov 04, 2026, 10:40 Save for later Save for later Crunchyroll Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News Dragon’s Dogma 2 is teaming up with the popular manga Delicious in Dungeon, giving fans the chance to add Laios and Marcille to their adventurer party. Delicious in Dungeon was one of the standout anime of 2024, with the fantasy show having one of the most unique takes on dungeon crawling. Instead of just slaying mythical beasts and calling it a day, warrior Laios and his trusty companions set about cooking everything that so much as moves. Article continues after ad No beast is safe from this food-loving party, and now Laios and elven mage Marcille are bringing their insatiable appetites to Dragon’s Dogma 2 as free recruitable companions complete with new outfits for fans to claim. It’s pretty exciting stuff, and fans of both the anime and manga couldn’t be happier with their addition to Capcom’s action RPG. Laios & Marcille head to Dragon’s Dogma 2 From today until January 29, 2027, Dragon’s Dogma 2 players on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC can recruit Official Pawns modeled after Laios and Marcille by visiting Riftstones in towns and other locations. (Nintendo Switch 2 players can claim them a week later, on November 12). Article continues after ad Article continues after ad The announcement has already drawn a lot of attention from the Delicious in Dungeon community, with fans praising Capcom for the new collab. “I can’t believe it, this is a dream collab I never thought would actually happen. The reason I started reading Danjon Meshi was that it reminded me of Dragon’s Dogma,” wrote one player. “Yes!!!! I literally spoke about this about a year ago, and to see this now is phenomenal,” added another. Related Dragon’s Dogma 2: Release date, trailer & more Delicious in Dungeon Season 2: First trailer, plot details & more Delicious In Dungeon anime releases episode 1 preview Article continues after ad Delicious in Dungeon arrives in the world of Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen with a special collaboration! 🥩 Hire Laios and Marcille as one-of-a-kind official Pawns and set off in search of adventure…and tasty meals! 👇 Check the reply for collab details! pic.twitter.com/os3yrdd7iT — Dragon's Dogma (@DragonsDogma) November 4, 2026 Just like in the manga/anime, Laios retains his swordsman class with the Fighter Vocation, while his magical partner Marcille has the Sorcerer Vocation. Players can also claim free outfits based on both characters by loading their save data in either Dragon’s Dogma 2 or Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen during the collaboration period. Both costumes will automatically appear in your in-game storage and can be equipped by your Arisen and Pawns. So, if you’re hungry for Delicious in Dungeon season 2, this crossover should help satisfy your appetite while you wait. Now, if only Capcom could add an official Frieren collab to the mix, then we’d be set for a perfect anime-themed adventure. title: LEGO Dragon Ball designer reveals hidden Shenron summoning Easter egg
summary: The designer behind Lego’s first Dragon Ball set has revealed a hidden Easter egg that lets fans collect all seven Dragon Balls before bringing Shenron to life.
details: Trending GTA 6 Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs TV & Movies Lego LEGO Dragon Ball designer reveals hidden Shenron summoning Easter egg by James Busby Published: Nov 18, 2026, 11:07 Save for later Save for later LEGO Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News The designer behind Lego ’s first Dragon Ball set has revealed a hidden Easter egg that lets fans collect all seven Dragon Balls before bringing Shenron to life. Collecting all seven Dragon Balls to summon a wish-granting dragon has been at the heart of Akira Toriyama’s series since its earliest adventures. While Lego’s Shenron & Goku set recreates that moment as a display piece, its designer also found a way to weave the anime’s iconic ritual into the building process. Article continues after ad Speaking to Dexerto, Lego Senior Model Designer Jae Won Lee revealed how a detail hidden inside the base lets builders follow in Goku’s footsteps. Lego’s Dragon Ball Easter egg starts before you build Shenron According to Lee, seven orange 2×2 round bricks serve a dual purpose within the set’s base. They help support the model, but their number and placement also give the opening stages of the build a connection to the anime. “As you build the base, you are essentially gathering all seven Dragon Balls in one place,” Lee explained. “Once the base is complete, you begin building Shenron, which symbolises the moment he is summoned. That’s the hidden Easter egg in this set.” Article continues after ad Article continues after ad These hidden bricks are separate from the visible Dragon Balls, which use ball joint elements to keep them in proportion with Shenron. Choosing Shenron alongside Kid Goku was also a deliberate nod to the original Dragon Ball series , with the team looking to capture the adventure that introduced fans to Toriyama’s world. LEGO “We wanted to capture Shenron’s majestic presence alongside Kid Goku’s innocence and adventurous spirit in a single model,” Lee said. Related Dragon Ball’s first-ever LEGO set leak reveals $180 Shenron and Goku Lego PlayStation & Astrobot sets revealed with hidden gaming Easter eggs Huge Lego Dragon Ball Z leak reveals nine upcoming sets Article continues after ad Rather than copying a single animation frame, the team drew inspiration from Shenron’s summoning scenes, particularly the way his body stretches into the sky and his commanding expression. However, recreating the green dragon’s iconic appearance proved to be the trickiest part of the design process. “The biggest challenge was recreating Shenron’s long, organic body using Lego elements,” said Lee. “Unlike many other dragons, the overall flow of his body is a defining part of his character. We needed to achieve natural-looking curves while maintaining structural stability and creating an appealing silhouette from different viewing angles.” Article continues after ad Article continues after ad LEGO Getting there involved numerous mock-ups and a wide range of poses, as the team experimented with how high Shenron should rise, which direction his body should follow, and how he should interact with Goku. When asked what his favorite part of the build is, Lee said it was Shenron’s face. “The face is where a character’s personality and emotion really come through. I love how a combination of small Lego elements and subtle changes in angles can create his distinctive, commanding expression. For me, the most satisfying moment is when you look at a collection of Lego bricks and suddenly see the character you remember from the anime.” Article continues after ad The Lego Shenron & Goku set is available to purchase now from Lego Stores and Lego’s website for $179.99. title: Japan’s JR East reveals new train company mascot character, online comments aren’t kind
summary: Filling the Suica Penguin’s shoes isn’t going to be easy. JR East/East Japan Railway Company hit a home run when it picked the original mascot for its Suica prepaid card system. Introduced at the same time as the system itself in 2001, the Suica Penguin was an instant success, giving a cute, approachable persona to […]
details: Filling the Suica Penguin’s shoes isn’t going to be easy . JR East/East Japan Railway Company hit a home run when it picked the original mascot for its Suica prepaid card system. Introduced at the same time as the system itself in 2001, the Suica Penguin was an instant success, giving a cute, approachable persona to what was at the time a novel way to pay for train fare and shopping purchases. In the two and a half decades since, the popularity of both Suica and its mascot have grown and grown, so it was a shock to many when, one year ago, JR East said it would be replacing the penguin with a new mascot . ▼ So long, Suica Penguin With the Suica system having become deeply integrated in so many people’s daily lives, the changeover is a big deal. JR East started by having a selection committee sift through artist proposals, then picking out three finalists which were revealed in September , with the winner to be decided through online voting. The candidates were a squirrel… …a rabbit… …and some kind of large-eared creature with a mole-like companion riding in its satchel . Polling ran from September 8 to September 23. JR East has now released the results, and the new Suica mascot is… …the rabbit…-ish-looking thing . This doesn’t appear to have been a narrow win, either. Out of a total 1,664,399 votes, 860,152 were for the rabbit . That’s 51.6 percent of the total, so unless one of the losing candidates got hardly any votes at all, the rabbit won by a substantial margin. This doesn’t mean, though, that everyone is emotionally onboard with the rail company’s new mascot . Reactions to the announcement tweet from JR East have been almost entirely negative, with many calling the character, with its vacant, expressionless eyes and seemingly pasted-on smile, far more creepy than cute. The purple color is also an issue for many, seeing as how it’s an attention-grabbing hue with no connection to JR East’s standard color designs (the company’s image color is green), and to many it looks like the character is suffering from poisoned status in an RPG video game. “That rabbit is seriously poisoned.” “Poison Bunny.” “Has me thinking of the Grimace Shake.” “Lo, I can feel only darkness within it.” “Man, they’re really going with the purple one…” “Was hoping for anything but this.” “This isn’t cute, and I can’t really tell what it’s supposed to be.” “I love it. For real. It’s cute.” “The penguin was cuter.” “It’s got a Teletubby kind of thing going on, and it’s freaking me out. Should have stuck with the penguin.” “Looks like some sort of monster from a horror video game.” “Yep, definitely gonna be some crying kids [when they see the character] at the station.” ／ Suicaの新たなイメージキャラクターが決定しました ～お客さまから愛称を募集します～ ＼ 2026年9月、Suicaの新たなイメージキャラクターのデザイン候補3案を発表し、お客さま投票を実施した結果、総得票数1,664,399票のうち860,152票を獲得した のキャラクターに決定しました … pic.twitter.com/LX5RMveCHE — JR 東日本ニュースリリース【公式】 (@JREast_News) November 18, 2026 The discrepancy between the rabbit being the clear favorite in voting but hardly anyone seeming to have anything to say about the design is surprising. One commenter wondered if the apparent landslide victory was a result of votes from those earnestly wanting a more conventionally cute character being split between the other options, while everyone wanting something weird or casting their vote as a joke then latched onto the rabbit with the unsettling expression . It’s also possible that the somewhat unfinished look of the squirrel (which lacks a visible outline) and the vagueness of the mole-and-friend design prevented them from really resonating with people wanting a conventionally cute mascot. Of course, there is precedent for a mascot who’s initially seen as creepy-looking to win over the public. When the Osaka Expo 2025 made its mascot a lump of irregularly shaped tissue and eyeballs, more than a few people were shocked, but Myaku-Myaku has gone on to build a fanbase , even after the event’s finish. A major shift in public opinion came after Myaku-Myaku’s voice, and association personality, was added, and there’s a possibility for the new Suica mascot to follow the same playbook. JR East is currently accepting suggestions for the new character’s name through its website here , and the form also includes sections for submitters to write what kind of personality they want the rabbit to have . Suggestions are being taken between now and December 15. Unlike with the mascot design, though, there will be no public voting this time, and instead the name will be selected by JR East. That’s probably for the best, since as of right now the most common suggestions online seem to be Bian (Japanese for “Option B,” as the rabbit was designated at its initial reveal), and Doku Usagi, which, as you can probably guess, means “Poison Bunny.” Source: JR East Top image: JR East Insert images: JR East ( 1 , 2 ) ● Want to hear about SoraNews24’s latest articles as soon as they’re published? title: Japan’s beautiful new Pokémon hotel room gives you and Dragonite a place to take a break
summary: Flying over to Fukui as part of your Japan trip? The prefecture’s Poké-bassador has a room all ready for you. Dragonite isn’t a Pokémon that likes to stay in one place very long. The Dragon/Flying Type is reportedly capable of circumnavigating the globe in just 16 hours, and it puts its wings to good use […]
details: Flying over to Fukui as part of your Japan trip? The prefecture’s Poké-bassador has a room all ready for you . Dragonite isn’t a Pokémon that likes to stay in one place very long. The Dragon/Flying Type is reportedly capable of circumnavigating the globe in just 16 hours, and it puts its wings to good use flying hither and yon. Of course, even Dragonite needs a place to spend the night when it’s roaming far from home, and it’s got a very special place to do that with Japan’s new Traveling Dragonite hotel room . You’ll find this unique offering in Fukui , the prefecture that Dragonite serves as tourism ambassador Pokémon for. Fukui is famous for the dinosaur fossils that have been excavated there, and with the Japanese word for dinosaur, kyoryu , translating literally as “terrifying dragon,” the draconic Dragonite was a natural choice to partner with the prefecture for the Pokémon Local Acts project, which seeks to shine a spotlight on beautiful and interesting parts of Japan that tourists might overlook if they’re only focusing on the largest cities and most famous sightseeing attractions. The Traveling Dragonite Room is located on the 11th floor of Awara Onsen Grandia Housen , a hotel in the Fukui hot spring town of Awara. Within the room, which can accommodate up to six guests, what look to be hundreds of Dragonites are waiting to greet you , as the Pokémon serves as the muse for the room’s tapestries and woven fabric pillowcases, bed runners, and cushion covers, all of which were created by local Fukui artisans using traditional methods. There are also Dragonite plushies on the beds, and while not specifically mentioned in the press release, there’s a chance that they could be yours to take home with you when you check out. The room consists of two sections, a bedroom area and a living room area, the latter with tatami reed flooring and a raised alcove in which more Dragonite artwork is displayed. As for why the room is on the 11th floor, it’s so that looking out the window at the expansive view of the nearby mountains and Sakai Plains will give you a perspective similar to what Dragonite would see on a Fukui flyover . The room has its own shower and bathtub, but with Grandia Housen being a hot spring inn, you’ll also want to take time to check out its traditional communal onsen baths, including the open-air rooftop ones. As you can see on the above map, Fukui is pretty far off the Tokyo-to-Osaka line that most visitors to Japan spend most of their time on. Getting off the so-called “golden route” can reward you with some still relatively hidden gems of the Japan travel scene, such as this lovely little town, this unusual workshop, or this very tasty meal, all of which we found in Fukui, and combining them with a night in a Dragonite-themed hotel room would make the whole side trip even better. Reservations are open now for the special Pokémon room through the Grandia Housen website, with the earliest available stays coming up soon on November 29. title: Life-size Gundam statue’s head returning to Tokyo neighborhood this month
summary: Odaiba welcomes back the head of the RX-0 Unicorn Gundam. East Japan is suffering from a serious shortage of life-size Gundams these days. Yokohama’s full-scale statue of the original RX-78 Gundam has been gone since the spring of 2024, when it was moved to Osaka for the Expo 2025 world’s fair (and which was dismantled […]
details: Odaiba welcomes back the head of the RX-0 Unicorn Gundam . East Japan is suffering from a serious shortage of life-size Gundams these days. Yokohama’s full-scale statue of the original RX-78 Gundam has been gone since the spring of 2024, when it was moved to Osaka for the Expo 2025 world’s fair (and which was dismantled after that event ended), and Tokyo’s 1:1 recreation of the Unicorn Gundam , which had been greeting visitors from around the world in the city’s Odaiba neighborhood since 2017, was taken down at the end of this past August . After anime’s most famous mecha series having some kind of large-scale presence in the Tokyo area for so long, for fans it definitely feels like there’s something missing now. Thankfully, while it’s still uncertain if or when Tokyo will be getting a new Gundam, statue, at least part of the Unicorn Gundam is coming back, as the life-size head unit will soon return to Odaiba for public display . Starting this weekend, the head of the RX-0 Unicorn Gundam will once again be back in the Festival Plaza outside the Diver City shopping/entertainment complex , just a short walk from Tokyo Teleport Station on the Rinkai Line or Daiba Station on the Yurikamome Line. While it will no longer sit at the top of the 19.7-meter (64.6-foot) tall robot like it used to, this new display will give fans a chance to see the head up-close and appreciate all the little details to its design, something that’ll be much easier to do at eye level than gazing up at it from far below like you used to have to. Famously, the Unicorn Gundam’s head unit can reconfigure itself, having a single unicorn-like horn in its “Unicorn Mode” and a more traditional split forehead crest in its “Destroy Mode.” This feature was replicated in the life-size statue, as shown in the video below, but it’s unclear if the head will be switching modes while on display by itself. This might not be the only Unicorn component that we’ll be seeing on display in the near future, either. “Right now, we can only display pieces,” says life-size Gundam project producer Kaori Shida, “so I’d like to at least have [them] hold something, move [their] position, or give [them] some kind of job to do.” It’s also too early to give up hope of ever seeing another Gundam Statue in east Japan. “Personally, I’d like to try a full remake of the original [RX-78 Gundam],” muses Masaki Kawahara, creative director of the Gundam Global Challenge initiative, “I think it would look cool if the maintenance hatch fully opened to reveal the inside, and then closed again to start the sequence.” The Unicorn Gundam head will be on display from November 21 , and is listed as being for a limited, although currently unspecified, time. Meanwhile, the head of the life-size RX-78 is scheduled to go on display in Osaka in early December , and for those in west Japan who want to see a life-size Gundam still standing tall, Fukuoka still has its Nu Gundam . details: Book a limited-time room with the beloved penguin mascot complete with free goodies, special foods, and a lottery to win a very large penguin figure. With JR East planning to “graduate” the penguin mascot of its rechargeable Suica ID card early next year , fans are beginning to get nostalgic for all things related to the wing-waving little friend. For many, it feels like a bittersweet farewell knowing that the penguin who accompanied them to school and work every day for dozens of years will no longer grace the front of new Suica cards. ▼ This little guy’s been with me since 2010–and shockingly, I haven’t lost him once since then. ©SoraNews24 Luckily, Hotel Metropolitan Tokyo Ikebukuro of JR East Hotels has unveiled a new concept room that will appeal to anyone wishing to celebrate the penguin’s departure in high style. From December 22, 2026 through March 30, 2027 , visitors can book a themed city-view room with a king-sized bed on the 22nd floor in which the penguin is taking its graduation trip to outer space. Only one room (maximum two people) is available per day, with check-in at 3 p.m. and check-out at 12 p.m. the following day. The room will come with not only out-of-this-world decorations but also original goods , including two sets of this multi-ring strap set that can be used as a shoulder strap for a smartphone case and is customizable with space-themed Suica penguin charms. Each guest will also receive a voucher to exchange for an adorable Suica Penguin Cake made from mascarpone and strawberry jelly. Just look at that little red bowtie! ▼ Suica Penguin Pancakes are another option for breakfast room service. Furthermore, guests can try their hand at a special capsule lottery , limited to one try per room, to win collaborative, not-for-sale items such as pouches, mug cups, acrylic stands, t-shirts, and even marzipan. For the final 15 days of the concept room beginning on March 16, the lottery will go all out with the addition of a special 95-centimeter (37.4-inch) penguin decoration , stand panels, plushies, bed runners, and tapestries for winning. Never fear if you’re coming from a distance because the hotel can ship any large items you score directly to your residence in Japan. Finally, a limited-time room service option will include a Suica Penguin Roast Beef and Camembert Cheeseburger for 3,000 yen (US$18.79). Hotel Metropolitan Tokyo Ikebukuro will begin taking reservations for the Suica penguin concept room on December 1 at 12 p.m. JST for dates of stay between December 22 and January 31 and on January 1 at 12 p.m. JST for dates of stay between February 1 and March 30. Rates are 47,800-62,100 yen for stays between December 22 and March 15 and 75,700 yen for stays between March 16 and March 30. For what it’s worth, I will always stand by the Suica penguin and not its new successor , thank you very much. details: Our reporter’s grandfather may not be here anymore, but he’s still showing her where to find great desserts . Our Japanese-language reporter Natsuki Gojo recently visited her mom, and while they were talking, Mom mentioned how much Natsuki’s grandfather loved a certain maker of Japanese confectionaries . The company, Gozasoro , was founded in Hyogo Prefecture in 1955 and really only makes one product, hockey puck-shaped cakes filled with anko (sweet bean jam), which some people call Imagawayaki , some people call obanyaki , and still other people call something else . You don’t stay in business for 70 years making only one thing unless you make it really well, and Gozasoro has been a stickler for quality ingredients from the very beginning. When the company started out, they charged 10 yen (US$0.06) per Imagawayaki, which was double the price most other shops sold theirs for at the time. Curious to try these sweets that had won her grandfather’s heart/stomach, Natsuki did some checking and found that Gozasoro has a branch inside the Takashimaya department store in downtown Tokyo’s Shinjuku neighborhood . Takashimaya is on the fancier side of Japanese department stores, and that extends to their food offerings, so Natsuki was prepared to maybe have to splurge a little to get some of Gozasoro’s Imagawayaki, since they obviously don’t sell for 10 yen anymore. Gozasoro branches pretty much always have a big glass window so that you can watch the staff cook up the treats while you wait in line to buy them. As you can see in the above photo, there are two fillings to choose from, regular/red anko, and white anko . If you’re having trouble deciding on which to buy, though, you may as well just get both. Why? Because even though Gozasoro isn’t selling Imagawayaki for 10 yen in 2026, they’re still an incredibly affordable snack at just 110 yen (US$0.69) each . Yep, for less than the cost of a bottle of water in vending machine will run you these days, you can get a freshly cooked Gozasoro Imagawayaki. With rising prices pummeling pocketbooks in Japan over the past few years, it’s very nice to see something that’s been so inflation-resistant. ▼ Even at that amazingly low price, the Shinjuku Takashimaya branch of Gozasoro still wraps its wares in the department store’s poshly patterned paper. After arriving home, Natsuki gave her Imagawayaki a quick stint in the microwave to reheat them, and then it was time for taste-testing . She started with the standard red anko version, and she was happy to find that it’s filled with an ample amount of sweet bean jam. With some lower-quality Imagawayaki you bite into them to find they’re mostly just dough with a tiny dollop of jam at the core, but the inside of Gozasoro’s is more than half anko, and that anko is very good, flavorfully sweet without being simplistically sugary . The cake itself, too, is excellent. Natsuki particularly liked the ever-so-slight crispness it’s cooked to, which makes for a great contrast with the soft anko inside . The white anko version looks identical on the outside… …but, of course, has white bean jam inside. Compared to the more common red version, white anko has a softer flavor and gentler sweetness , making for a more refined impression while still being an approachable, crowd-pleasing taste. Imagawayaki aren’t particularly tiny snacks, and most people eat just one in a sitting. These were so good, though, that before Natsuki realized it, she gobbled them both down and was feeling both rather full and extremely happy. There was just one thing puzzling her: despite her mom telling her that her grandfather had loved Gozasoro, Natsuki couldn’t remember him ever inviting her to snack on their Imagawayaki together . This may have been Natsuki’s fault, though. Thinking back, Natsuki remembers really loving anpan (bread buns filled with anko) when she was a very little kid, until an incident that occurred at swimming school. Somehow her class had ended up with a surplus of snacks, and Natsuki ate so many anpan that she ended up feeling sick, which turned her off anko for the rest of her childhood, and her lack of enthusiasm for it probably meant her grandfather figured she wouldn’t be interested in Gozasoro’s desserts. It wasn’t until Natsuki got older, and after her grandfather passed away, that she once again developed a taste for anko, and now that she’s got no beef with sweet bean jam, she’s happy to be able to enjoy the same treats that he did. She wishes they could have shared some, so the next time she visits his grave, she’s planning to bring some Gozasoro Imagawayaki as an offering for him.
