title: FamilyMart’s “physical AI” robot workers getting chilly reception in Japan
summary: Sure, it doesn’t do much, but it’s a robot! Even as AI is still in its early stages, many eager start-ups are looking at the next big thing, which they have dubbed “physical AI.” That really just means robots controlled by AI, but it seems to be a buzzword that piggybacks on the name recognition […]
details: Sure, it doesn’t do much, but it’s a robot! Even as AI is still in its early stages, many eager start-ups are looking at the next big thing, which they have dubbed “physical AI.” That really just means robots controlled by AI, but it seems to be a buzzword that piggybacks on the name recognition of “AI” itself. In Japan, one company that has made great strides in actually putting physical AI to the test in real-world applications is Telexistence. Over the past few years, they have been developing robots to alleviate the labor shortages many convenience stores have been facing . After a fair bit of testing, major convenience store chain FamilyMart announced that, starting next year, they would begin rolling out physical AI drink stockers to every location in Japan . These are AI-powered mechanical claws that are installed behind the drink section and constantly refill cans and bottles. コンビニ大手のファミリーマートは、飲料を自動で補充するフィジカルAIを活用したロボットを本格導入する方針です。どんなロボットなのでしょうか。 https://t.co/LvhlAmeiUY #nhk_video pic.twitter.com/iNwK0u3i5u — NHKニュース (@nhk_news) November 12, 2026 Watching this system in action, two things are certain to spring to mind. First, it’s quite slow , but realistically, that should be fine since, unlike a human who would pop in and fill everything at once in a couple of minutes, this thing is working nonstop, around the clock. As long as it outpaces the rate people are buying drinks, it should be fine. The more problematic observation is that the robot is moving drinks from a shelf to the fridge, which begs the question of how that first shelf was stocked. If a human is required to fill the shelf used by the robot to move the drinks into the fridge, then why not get the human to just stock the fridge directly? According to FamilyMart, adoption of this system will reduce a human’s beverage stocking time by 70 percent. However, since beverage stocking is just one part of an employee’s many duties, it’s unclear how much real-world work that would equate to. Many readers of the news online were unconvinced it would amount to much in comments. People from both inside the industry and out came forward in saying they felt these machines have failed to impress. “The shelves are restocked by robots from shelves restocked by humans. That’s called doing the same work twice.” “It has to be fully automated, starting with opening the cardboard boxes. Otherwise, it’s pointless!” “Why not just make it a big vending machine, where you push a button and the drink comes out?” “I’m curious about how deliveries are handled, but more importantly… IT’S SOOOOOO SLOW!” “I was thinking this was a good idea because part-timers sometimes do horrible things. But someone could just hack into these and make them do horrible things too.” “It’s slow, but if it runs automatically all the time, I guess that’s fine. Guess I’ll be able to take my time at work a little more.” “I’ve worked with this robot before. I have to restock the shelves behind it, putting a set number of items in specific spots. It’s such a pain in the butt. The rails on the floor it uses are dangerous for humans to trip on. It bugs out a lot, and each time I have to use an iPad or call someone. Humans are faster, and it was such a waste I was literally crying.” “That is 100 times slower than I even expected.” “Is there a need for the robotic arm? Why not just tilt the shelves to slide new bottles in?” “I am the owner of two FamilyMart franchise stores. I think the installation cost for this machine is 1.2 million yen. Considering most stores don’t even generate a net profit of 100,000 yen a month, how could any store afford these? None of the stores are asking for this stuff. The priority should be helping franchises who are struggling with soaring labor costs!” “I laughed at the ‘physical AI’ part. It’s neither physical nor AI.” In defense of the people behind these robots, from what I’ve read, this is just one component of a much more integrated system that manages various aspects of running a convenience store, from cleaning floors to managing inventory. Perhaps when viewed as a whole, it would be more useful. ▼ Their bag bot looks promising, but still has a way to go. Unfortunately, that important detail required extra research to find out, so to most readers it appears as if this single claw was being triumphantly paraded out as the solution to all convenience stores’ problems. Honestly, I feel like if they’d stuck with the giant cat-man design they started with, it would have gotten a much warmer reception overall. title: Online scammers beware, one man is coming for your fried rice recipes… all of them
summary: Revenge is a dish best served fried with just the right seasoning. While AI is increasingly becoming a part of society, there’s still a lot of confusion about exactly how it fits into our lives. Making ugly restaurant menus is all well and good, but how can we really harness its potential to make the […]
details: Revenge is a dish best served fried with just the right seasoning. While AI is increasingly becoming a part of society, there’s still a lot of confusion about exactly how it fits into our lives. Making ugly restaurant menus is all well and good, but how can we really harness its potential to make the future a better place to live? This is a question one of SoraNews24’s greatest minds, Go Hatori , has long wrestled with and finally has an answer for. Long-time readers may recall that Go frequently tangles with online scammers of all types. He fearlessly engages with them and turns the tables by earning their trust instead, only to deprive them of their precious time on this planet with banal conversation that goes nowhere . Thus, the scammer becomes the scammed. It’s not just something he does for funny articles either. Go has seriously established himself as a leading authority on online fraud in Japan, having written books, provided his expertise on TV, and given numerous lectures on the topic of online safety. Although there are lots of laughs along the way, his dedication to this pressing social issue is certainly no joke. Now, armed with artificial intelligence, Go is planning a counteroffensive against con artists unlike any ever seen. He has converted his apartment into the First Recipe Division of the Fried Rice Unit (FRU), a non-governmental agency devoted to seeking out all online grifters, befriending them, and then stealing their fried rice recipes once their guard has been lowered . How does he do this? Well, FRU is powered by a state-of-the-art-circa-2020 M1 Mac mini that he bought secondhand along with some wireless peripherals. Due to the nature of its covert activities, FRU needs to operate in a completely separate environment from Go’s daily activities. The Mac mini does this on its own with Muse and ChatGPT agents. Go has set them up to lure in scammers via Instagram DMs into a dedicated account on the Japanese texting app Line. From there, the AIs engage in pleasant conversations with the crooks, all the while gently nudging the conversation towards fried rice . Once a scammer is on the hook, the AIs alert Go, who takes over personally and secures the recipe. The main work is all done automatically, so he never bothered to get a monitor for the Mac mini, but he hooked it up to a projector for the occasional times when his personal input and maintenance are required. It has the added effect of looking really cool, which is a must for any counter-intelligence agency. As Go stood back and gazed at his new FRU setup, he felt a slight pang. In doing this, he had become the thing he had sworn to fight. He had become the boss of a scamming ring. Still, every conversation his FRU agents Chloe (Muse) and Nancy (ChatGPT) tie up a con artist with is one less conversation had with a potential victim. Getting a fried rice recipe from them in the process is just the icing on the cake. But more than that, Go found through his own dealings with these people that getting them to offer up a fried rice recipe was a rare glimpse into the real person behind the lies . Perhaps in doing so, it reminds them of what it means to be human and to have compassion for others. But even if it doesn’t, Go can still try some new dishes. ▼ The FRU Central Mainframe also blends in seamlessly with Go’s decor. So, swindlers and cheats of the world, you have been warned. The FRU is out there and, thanks to the relentless determination only a machine can provide, it will not stop until it has robbed all of you of your fried rice recipes . In fact, as of this writing, Go has already stolen one and will share it in an upcoming fraud food review! title: Starbucks Japan adds new Tiramisu Latte to the menu for a limited time
summary: Exclusive dessert drink is the winter warmer we’ve been waiting for. It was only the other day when we received the glorious news that Starbucks would be releasing a special limited-edition Matcha Tiramisu Frappuccino in Japan. Now, the chain is surprising us yet again, with the announcement that it will be adding another new drink […]
details: Exclusive dessert drink is the winter warmer we’ve been waiting for. It was only the other day when we received the glorious news that Starbucks would be releasing a special limited-edition Matcha Tiramisu Frappuccino in Japan. Now, the chain is surprising us yet again, with the announcement that it will be adding another new drink to the menu, and this time it’s a hot Tiramisu Latte , which aims to capture the indulgent taste of the original dessert. Designed as a holiday release for the end-of-year festive season, the Tiramisu Latte combines the rich aroma and depth of espresso with smooth mascarpone cream to create a drink that recreates the layered flavours of coffee-soaked sponge biscuits and mascarpone. Like a regular tiramisu, the drink displays a beautiful balance between creamy sweetness and pleasantly bitter coffee flavours and is topped with a dusting of cocoa powder to finish. A dash of white mocha-flavoured syrup and smooth steamed milk is also added to the mix, while the top layer of mascarpone cream adds richness and mellowness to the drink, softening the espresso’s bitter notes. The finishing touch is a dusting of Dark Frappuccino Powder, which adds a hint of bitterness and helps give the beverage a flavour reminiscent of the real dessert. The result is a rich, smooth and subtly bittersweet drink designed to bring a little extra indulgence to the holiday season. For even more holiday cheer, Starbucks will be bringing its “ Merry & Meet Holiday Bingo Party ” campaign to life with special pop-up events at two stores in Tokyo and Osaka. The events invite visitors to step into the world of the holiday bingo campaign, with special decorations and large photo panels featuring Bearista, the brand’s beloved bear mascot, as the host of the holiday bingo party. These festive photo spots will be installed at the Starbucks Coffee Shibuya cocoti branch in Tokyo from 5-13 December, and at Starbucks Coffee LINKS Umeda 2F in Osaka from 27 November to 6 December. Customers who show the Holiday Bingo Party screen in the Starbucks app at either participating store will also receive an original sticker, while stocks remain available. As for the Tiramisu Latte, it will be on the menu from 618 yen (US$4.12), and will be available at Starbucks stores across Japan from 20 November. title: Foreign tourist missing after off-season Mt. Fuji hike, father reportedly offering reward to find him/his body
summary: Two of three friends made the right decision to call off their Mt. Fuji hiking plans. In the first week of this month, a Chinese tourist in his 20s arrived in Japan with two friends. The trio then made their way to Yamamanshi, drawn to the prefecture, like many others, by Mt. Fuji, which straddles […]
details: Two of three friends made the right decision to call off their Mt. Fuji hiking plans . In the first week of this month, a Chinese tourist in his 20s arrived in Japan with two friends . The trio then made their way to Yamamanshi, drawn to the prefecture, like many others, by Mt. Fuji , which straddles Yamanashi’s border with Shizuoka Prefecture. The three didn’t go to Mt. Fuji to appreciate the sight of it from afar, though, but with the intention to climb Japan’s tallest mountain . However, Mt. Fuji’s climbing season has been finished for the year since early September , which is something the man’s friends weren’t aware of until after they got to Yamanashi. That’s honestly kind of shocking. Despite how enticingly gentle its slopes may look from a distance, summiting Mt. Fuji is a strenuous endeavor, and one that can be very dangerous in the off-season, when the weather is colder, daylight hours shorter, and support facilities such as mountain huts aren’t operating. In recent years there have been an increasing number of rescue missions that had to be carried out in order to save off-season hikers , and pretty much any reputable website with Mt. Fuji climbing information will start with information on when the climbing season begins and ends. As surprising as the gap in knowledge may have been, the man’s friends at least showed good wisdom by then deciding to call off their hike. The man himself, though, was now determined to go it alone. On the morning of November 8, he set off from the fifth station of Mt. Fuji’s Yoshida Trail , where regular road access ends. He was apparently in good spirits, sending text messages and videos to his friends who’d declined to make the climb with him. Unfortunately, that was the last time anyone has heard from him . As of November 17, the man hasn’t returned or contacted any of his friends or family. According to one of the friends who came with him to Japan, he wasn’t equipped with any specialized winter hiking gear such as crampons for extra traction while walking potentially icy sections of the trail. He didn’t have a tent either, which is especially concerning since, what with it being the off-season, there are no mountain huts or other shelters that are currently staffed and operating on the mountain. ▼ “It is regrettable that someone would make the decision to recklessly climb [Mt. Fuji] while the mountain is closed to hikers,” said Fujiyoshida mayor Shigeru Horiuchi while discussing the situation. Police are continuing to search for the missing man, but have found no sign of him yet. On November 13, five days after he went missing, the man’s father arrived in Japan . According to Chinese media reports, he has offered a reward of 500,000 yuan (approximately US$75,000) to anyone who can find his son while he’s still alive, and 100,000 should anyone discover his body . The whole thing isn’t going over well with online commenters in Japan, whose reactions have included: “First pay for the cost of the search and rescue operation .” “If you’ve got many to toss around, give it straight to the rescue workers who’re looking for your son.” “How does a guy like that even manage to make any friends in the first place?” “Just leave him up there. Doesn’t matter what country you’re from. If you try to climb the mountain during the off-season, whatever happens is on you.” “I hope this doesn’t end up making other people run off to Mt. Fuji to look for him and then end up needing to be rescued themselves.” As for that last point, once again it should be stressed that hiking Mt. Fuji can be incredibly dangerous right now, so going to look for the son yourself really isn’t a bright idea, and that’s even without getting into the question of whether or not the Japanese authorities would even allow someone to accept/keep a reward earned through doing something you’re not supposed to (hiking Mt. Fuji at this time of year). Hopefully the son can still be found and returned home safely, but for now this a solemn reminder to stay off of Mt. Fuji in the off-season. Studio Ghibli has long been a champion of Japanese culture, both in its movie storylines and its merchandise ranges. Right now, that support for Japan and its culture is clearly evident in a new release from the studio’s GBL brand , which specialises in cool streetwear influenced by American fashion, and it’s called the Princess Mononoke Velveteen Sukajan jacket . As the name suggests, this new product celebrates the studio’s 1997 animated feature film Princess Mononoke , with a design that includes a cute nod to the year of the movie’s release. ▼ A kodama forest spirit sits in place of the second “9” in 1997. The sukajan is a Japanese souvenir jacket , traditionally decorated with elaborate embroidery depicting motifs like Japanese landscapes, animals and mythical creatures. The style became popular among American servicemen stationed in Japan after World War II, specifically in the area of Yokosuka in Tokyo’s neighbouring Kanagawa Prefecture, who commissioned embroidered jackets as souvenirs. Today, sukajan represent a unique facet of Japanese streetwear, making it a perfect item for the American-influenced GBL brand. This particular sukajan is an updated version of a jacket originally released in 2019. This new design features a large image of heroine San riding giant wolf Moro on the back… ▼ … and images of the boar god Okkoto (known as “Okkoto-nushi” in Japanese) embroidered on the front. ▼ The deep moss-green colour is inspired by the forests in the film. The jacket has a convenient inner pocket, and the bright terracotta lining contrasts nicely with the vivid green, creating a stylish flash of colour when the jacket is unzipped. Another unique feature is the fabric – unlike the shiny satin frequently associated with sukajan, this version is made from velveteen, which gives it a softer look, with just a hint of sheen. ▼ It also has insulating padding, making it suitable for colder weather, and a beautiful tag featuring deer god Shishigami. Other details include a ribbed collar, cuffs and hem, a YKK zipper and slash pockets on the front. The embroidery is made using a dimensional hand-guided technique, giving the designs a raised, textured appearance. The jacket is available in four unisex sizes, from S to XL, and the model in these photos is 173 centimetres (5 feet 8 inches) tall and wears a size XL. Sukajan are generally made to last and are priced as such, with this one retailing for 39,600 yen (US$248). While the jacket was made available online from 14 November, it’s set to be stocked at GBL retail stores in Japan from 21 November. title: Tokyo’s Shibuya Sakurazaka cherry blossom street to be decommissioned, number of trees to increase
summary: Shibuya’s cherry blossom hill to live on and become pinker than ever. Usually, when people think of Tokyo’s Shibuya neighborhood, they think of the famous Shibuya Scramble intersection and statue of faithful dog Hachiko, plus trendy fashion shops, lively bars, and tourist-friendly pop culture specialty stores. All of those things are indeed iconic parts of […]
details: Shibuya’s cherry blossom hill to live on and become pinker than ever . Usually, when people think of Tokyo’s Shibuya neighborhood, they think of the famous Shibuya Scramble intersection and statue of faithful dog Hachiko , plus trendy fashion shops, lively bars, and tourist-friendly pop culture specialty stores . All of those things are indeed iconic parts of Shibuya, but they’re all located on the northwest side of Shibuya Station. Meanwhile, if you head just a block or two southwest from the station, you’ll find something you might not expect in a part of the city known for urban exuberance: an ascending street lined with beautiful cherry blossom trees . ▼ It’s actually a really pretty place even when the sakura aren’t in bloom. The road is called Sakurazaka , meaning “cherry blossom hill,” a much more poetic moniker than its other name, Ward Road 1032. That designation is important, though, as the Shibuya Ward government has announced that it will be decommissioning Sakurazaka as part of the ongoing property development construction that’s been taking place in the district . The disparity in economic activity between the area to the northwest of Shibuya Station and those on its other sides hasn’t escaped the notice of real estate investors. In recent years, a number of new commercial and office high-rises developments have gone up, such as the Hikarie, Shibuya Scramble Square, and Shibuya Stream buildings to the east and southeast of the station. Now developers are turning their attention in earnest to the area to the southwest of the station, for a development to be called “Next Shibuya Sakurazaka.” ▼ Shibuya Station (渋谷駅) and the site of Next Shibuya Sakurazaka (marked in pink) The development will be subdivided into three sections, currently called Blocks A, B, and C. Block A is planned to be a 35-floor skyscraper with offices, shops, a concert hall with a capacity of 2,000 attendees, and a bus terminal . However, Block A is going to be built, map-wise, right on top of Sakurazaka . Marked in blue on the map below are Sakurazaka (Ward Road 1032) and two perpendicular ward-administered roads within the current street network… …and here are the sites that Blocks A, B, and C are going to be built on. “Downtown Tokyo loses cherry blossom road in order to build shops and offices” would be a story that would induce tears, anger, or some combined result of moist rage among many people, but there is a silver lining to all this . Yes, Sakurazaka is going to be decommissioned as a ward-administered road, and the property developers do plan to build over the existing road’s asphalt. What they’re not planning to do, though, is get rid of the cherry blossom trees . Instead, as shown in the preview image above, the existing sakura are being incorporated into the new development’s design, in what appears will be a walkable, publicly accessible part of the center. What’s more, the plan is to actually increase the number of cherry blossom tress . The street currently has 29 trees, but the developers want Block A to have 40 to 50, largely expanding the amount of sakura to be seen. It’s not clear if each and every tree on Sakurazaka will be retained in its current position, as some may need to be removed for safety reasons based on their age. Nevertheless, it’s clear that the developers aren’t looking to just chop them all down and pour dull gray concrete all across the hill. The decommissioning of Ward Road 1032 isn’t going to be a great loss for transportation infrastructure either . Originally, the road was supposed to stretch to Jiyu-dori Street in Meguro Ward’s Higashigaoka neighborhood, but instead it tapers and dissolves long before reaching that point. That initial plan was created not long after the end of World War II, and in the ensuing years that it’s been stalled several other roads that serve that purpose have been built, leading the Shibuya Ward administration to deem it unnecessary in its most recent once-a-decade reevaluation. ▼ Shibuya Sakurazaka at night this past spring All things considered, it’s probably not such a bad turn of events for Shibuya’s Sakurazaka, and being an attractive feature of a commercial center gives the developers incentive to make sure the trees are properly cared for. That said, the atmosphere is probably going to be different than the more organic community vibe Sakurazaka has right now, so thankfully construction isn’t scheduled to start until 2030 , meaning you’ve still got a few sakura season chances to see it as it is. title: Skip and Loafer regresa en abril de 2027 y Mitsumi ya encontró su lugar en Tokio
summary: Skip and Loafer regresa en abril de 2027 con un nuevo tráiler, imagen promocional y dos compañeros de clase que se unirán a la vida escolar de Mitsumi.
details: Anime Skip and Loafer regresa en abril de 2027 y Mitsumi ya encontró su lugar en Tokio El nuevo tráiler presenta una partida de boliche, chocolates caseros y dos compañeros que llegan para el segundo año. Kenji hace 1 hora 0 Comentarios ADS Después de cuatro años de espera, finalmente podremos volver a disfrutar de esos pequeños momentos escolares que hacen tan especial a Skip and Loafer . La segunda temporada del anime presentó su primer tráiler completo y una nueva imagen promocional , confirmando que Mitsumi Iwakura y sus amigos regresarán a la televisión en abril de 2027 . Y aunque esta historia no necesita grandes batallas ni villanos para mantenernos pendientes, parece que una simple partida de boliche será suficiente para recordarnos por qué extrañábamos tanto a sus personajes. El nuevo avance, publicado el 16 de noviembre, muestra a Mitsumi disfrutando de diferentes actividades con sus compañeros de preparatoria. Entre las escenas destacan un torneo de boliche y un intercambio de chocolates hechos a mano , además de los encuentros cotidianos que caracterizan a esta comedia escolar. Pero uno de los detalles más interesantes aparece cuando Mitsumi reflexiona sobre su vida en Tokio y reconoce que aquel lugar, que al principio le resultaba tan desconocido, finalmente se ha convertido en un espacio al que siente que pertenece. Una pequeña frase que resume bastante bien cuánto ha cambiado desde su llegada a la ciudad. Dos nuevos compañeros llegarán a la vida de Mitsumi La segunda temporada también incorporará nuevos personajes, pues Mitsumi y sus amigos comenzarán su segundo año de preparatoria. Entre los estudiantes que conoceremos se encuentran Chieri Yasaka y Kiyohiko Ujiie , quienes tendrán sus propias dificultades para relacionarse con los demás. Reina Ueda interpretará a Chieri Yasaka , una muchacha que parece adorable y delicada, pero que también disfruta confundiendo deliberadamente a los chicos interesados en ella. Aunque algunas de sus compañeras no aprueban su comportamiento, Chieri aparenta no preocuparse demasiado por las críticas. La actriz explicó que le llamó especialmente la atención la sonrisa de su personaje, pues le provoca curiosidad descubrir qué sentimientos esconde. También señaló que percibe cierta soledad detrás de la manera tan calculada en que Chieri se relaciona con otras personas, por lo que espera comprender mejor su personalidad a lo largo de la historia. Por otra parte, Yuto Takenaka dará voz a Kiyohiko Ujiie , un estudiante de cabello largo y lentes que suele expresarse con educación, aunque tiene una personalidad bastante complicada. Su tendencia a decir lo que piensa sin demasiados filtros puede ocasionar conflictos innecesarios con quienes lo rodean. Takenaka describió a su personaje como alguien que lucha constantemente con sus sentimientos de inferioridad, inseguridades y orgullo. El actor adelantó que uno de sus principales intereses será mostrar cómo cambia Kiyohiko después de conocer a Mitsumi y sus compañeros. Skip and Loafer continuará con su historia de amistades y crecimiento La adaptación seguirá contando con P.A.WORKS como estudio de animación , mientras que Kotomi Deai estará a cargo de la dirección y participará en la composición de la serie junto con Yoko Yonaiyama. Manami Umeshita regresará como diseñadora de personajes. También volverán las voces principales de la primera temporada, incluyendo a Tomoyo Kurosawa como Mitsumi Iwakura y Akinori Egoshi como Sosuke Shima . El elenco contará nuevamente con Yuka Terasaki como Mika Egashira, Maaya Uchida como Yuzuki Murashige y Megumi Han como Makoto Kurume, entre otros integrantes. Para quienes todavía no conocen la franquicia, Skip and Loafer sigue a Mitsumi, una estudiante brillante que deja su pequeño pueblo en la prefectura de Ishikawa para ingresar a una prestigiosa preparatoria de Tokio. Aunque tiene grandes planes para su futuro, pronto descubre que obtener buenas calificaciones no significa necesariamente entender cómo funcionan las relaciones sociales . Su personalidad sincera y sus pequeños tropiezos terminan acercándola a compañeros muy diferentes entre sí. Así, la historia explora las amistades, las inseguridades y esos momentos aparentemente insignificantes que pueden cambiar la manera en que una persona se ve a sí misma. El anime adapta el manga de Misaki Takamatsu , publicado desde octubre de 2018 en la revista Monthly Afternoon de Kodansha. Su primera temporada se estrenó en abril de 2023 y consiguió llamar la atención por su tratamiento de los personajes y su cálida representación de la vida escolar. Por ahora, el estreno de la segunda temporada está confirmado para abril de 2027 , aunque todavía no se ha revelado el día exacto ni la cantidad de episodios. Mientras tanto, el nuevo avance deja claro que Mitsumi seguirá aprendiendo que crecer también significa encontrarse con personas que no siempre son tan fáciles de entender. ¿Qué tienes más ganas de ver en la segunda temporada de Skip and Loafer : cómo evoluciona la relación entre Mitsumi y Shima o las nuevas amistades y conflictos que llegarán con sus compañeros de segundo año? title: The Days of Diamond tendrá anime: ser demasiado bueno en béisbol también duele
summary: The Days of Diamond anuncia su adaptación al anime con Lapin Track. La historia sigue a un prodigio del béisbol cuyo talento termina alejándolo de sus amigos.
details: Anime The Days of Diamond tendrá anime: ser demasiado bueno en béisbol también duele Un niño con talento extraordinario descubre que ganar siempre puede ser la mejor manera de quedarse solo. Yuna hace 12 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS Imagínate ser tan bueno en un deporte que nadie quiera jugar contigo. Suena como un problema que muchos desearían tener, pero para Jiro Ayasegawa es una realidad bastante dolorosa. Ahora, su historia llegará a la televisión, pues se anunció oficialmente que el manga The Days of Diamond tendrá una adaptación al anime , producida por el estudio Lapin Track. La noticia llegó acompañada de una primera imagen promocional y una ilustración especial de su autor. El anuncio se realizó el 17 de noviembre mediante la apertura del sitio oficial de la adaptación, conocida en Japón como Diamond no Kouzai . Por ahora, no se ha revelado una fecha de estreno , pero ya se confirmó al equipo principal que llevará a la pantalla esta peculiar historia sobre béisbol, amistad y las consecuencias de poseer un talento extraordinario. La primera imagen muestra a Jiro de espaldas, vistiendo el uniforme de un lanzador con el número de un as. Por otra parte, el mangaka Ohashi Hirai compartió una ilustración con los integrantes del equipo Bambies disfrutando de una comida juntos, en una escena mucho más alegre que contrasta con los conflictos que plantea la obra. Un niño que solamente quería divertirse jugando béisbol La historia de The Days of Diamond sigue a Jiro Ayasegawa , un niño que nació con habilidades físicas extraordinarias. Es capaz de destacar en prácticamente cualquier deporte que intenta practicar, superando con facilidad a compañeros que llevan años entrenando para mejorar sus resultados. Sin embargo, lo que debería ser una enorme ventaja termina convirtiéndose en su principal problema. Su talento es tan descomunal que constantemente deja atrás a los demás , provocando frustración entre quienes intentan competir contra él. Aunque Jiro no tiene malas intenciones, acaba sintiéndose cada vez más aislado. Todo cambia cuando descubre a los Adachi Bambies , un pequeño equipo infantil de béisbol que no destaca precisamente por sus victorias. Sus integrantes simplemente disfrutan jugando juntos, sin obsesionarse con convertirse en grandes estrellas. Para Jiro, que nunca había encontrado un lugar donde pudiera sentirse como uno más, esta experiencia representa algo completamente nuevo. Por primera vez comienza a comprender que el deporte puede tratarse de compartir momentos con sus amigos y no solamente de demostrar quién es mejor. Sin embargo, su extraordinaria habilidad como lanzador pronto llama la atención de otras personas, llevándolo a formar parte de la selección japonesa sub-12. Así comienza una historia que no solamente muestra el crecimiento de un prodigio deportivo, sino también las consecuencias que su talento tiene sobre quienes lo rodean . Porque mientras algunos ven a Jiro como una promesa del béisbol, otros deben enfrentarse a sus propias limitaciones y a la posibilidad de que sus sueños nunca se hagan realidad. El estudio de Shoshimin Series producirá el anime La adaptación estará dirigida por Takakazu Nagatomo en el estudio Lapin Track , conocido por producciones como Shoshimin Series y You and I Are Polar Opposites . Chigusa Kiyota participará como asistente de dirección, mientras que Atsushi Saito se encargará del diseño de personajes y Teruko Utsumi supervisará la composición de la serie y los guiones. En un mensaje compartido durante el anuncio, Nagatomo reconoció que el manga original le ha parecido especialmente impactante por la manera en que representa el talento de Ayasegawa y los conflictos que provoca entre los demás personajes. El director aseguró que su equipo está trabajando para trasladar esas emociones a la animación sin perder la intensidad de la obra. Por su parte, Utsumi destacó la importancia de recordar que cada personaje tiene una vida, un pasado y un futuro propios, algo que intentó conservar durante la escritura de los guiones. El manga original de Ohashi Hirai comenzó su publicación en febrero de 2023 dentro de la revista Weekly Young Jump de Shueisha. Desde entonces ha conseguido superar los 2 millones de copias en circulación y obtuvo el primer lugar en la categoría masculina de la guía Kono Manga ga Sugoi! 2024 . La obra también ha atravesado varias pausas durante su serialización. La más reciente comenzó en enero de 2026 y terminó con su regreso el 4 de junio. Actualmente cuenta con diez volúmenes recopilatorios publicados, mientras que el volumen 11 llegará a las tiendas japonesas el 18 de noviembre . Sus capítulos también pueden leerse digitalmente en inglés mediante MANGA Plus. Por ahora, los responsables del anime no han revelado el reparto de voces, la cantidad de episodios ni su posible distribución internacional. Pero su primera imagen ya deja bastante claro que esta no será simplemente otra historia sobre un equipo que quiere ganar el campeonato. ¿Crees que tener un talento tan grande como el de Jiro sería una bendición, o preferirías ser un jugador normal y disfrutar del béisbol sin terminar alejando a todos tus amigos? title: Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi vuelve en 2027: ¡ni los demonios se salvan del amor!
summary: Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi confirma su segunda temporada para 2027 con un nuevo tráiler, imagen promocional y cuatro personajes que se unirán al romance.
details: Anime Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi vuelve en 2027: ¡ni los demonios se salvan del amor! La demonio más fácil de conquistar regresa con cuatro nuevos personajes, un tráiler y más problemas románticos. Kenji hace 33 minutos 0 Comentarios ADS Se suponía que Kanan había llegado al mundo humano para devorar almas, pero terminó descubriendo que enamorarse puede ser mucho más complicado que cualquier misión demoníaca. Y parece que sus problemas sentimentales apenas están comenzando, pues se confirmó que la segunda temporada de Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi se estrenará en 2027 , acompañada de un nuevo tráiler, una imagen promocional y cuatro incorporaciones al elenco. La continuación llevará por título Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi 2 EASY , conservando el peculiar sentido del humor que caracteriza a esta comedia romántica. El anuncio se realizó el 17 de noviembre a través del sitio oficial del anime, donde también se presentaron los diseños de los nuevos personajes. El primer video promocional permite escuchar las voces de las nuevas integrantes del reparto, quienes llegarán para complicar todavía más las relaciones entre los protagonistas. Porque, aparentemente, una demonio que apenas está aprendiendo a tener novio necesita más personas que puedan poner a prueba su paciencia. Cuatro nuevas chicas se unen a Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi Una de las principales novedades es la incorporación de cuatro personajes que tendrán presencia en la segunda temporada. Las actrices confirmadas son las siguientes: Misato Matsuoka como Tekka Shinryuji. Miku Ito como Hanako Ohanabatake. Miyu Tomita como Lily Kageno. Lynn como Koko Kyogi. Las cuatro actrices compartieron mensajes sobre su participación en el anime. Matsuoka describió a Tekka como una mujer especialmente firme, mientras que Ito destacó la personalidad alegre, inocente y directa de Hanako, así como su relación con Lily, cuyos contrastes prometen momentos interesantes. Por su parte, Tomita confesó que Lily representa un tipo de personaje al que no está acostumbrada y que inicialmente tuvo dudas sobre si sería adecuada para interpretarla. Sin embargo, explicó que durante las grabaciones logró encontrar una manera de expresar su personalidad que terminó resultándole bastante natural. Finalmente, Lynn adelantó que la segunda temporada contará con un elenco todavía más numeroso y excéntrico , por lo que los espectadores pueden esperar situaciones especialmente caóticas. También está confirmado el regreso de Aoi Koga como Kanan Takakiyo y Seiichiro Yamashita como Yoji Kyogi , quienes continuarán protagonizando esta peculiar relación entre una demonio y un estudiante humano. Una demonio que quería devorar almas y terminó consiguiendo novio Para quienes todavía no conocen la franquicia, Kanan-sama wa Akumade Choroi , también conocida como Mistress Kanan is Devilishly Easy , cuenta la historia de Kanan Takakiyo , una demonio que se infiltra en una preparatoria humana con la intención de conseguir almas jóvenes para alimentarse. Su primera víctima debería ser Yoji Kyogi, un estudiante aparentemente normal que despierta su interés. Sin embargo, las cosas toman un rumbo completamente inesperado cuando ambos terminan estableciendo una relación romántica , convirtiendo a la supuesta cazadora de almas en una muchacha que apenas sabe cómo reaccionar ante sus propios sentimientos. El verdadero problema es que Kanan, a pesar de haber vivido durante miles de años, nunca había experimentado el amor. Por eso, actividades tan sencillas como caminar juntos, tomarse de las manos o tener una cita pueden convertirse en situaciones verdaderamente desesperantes para ella. La segunda temporada continuará desarrollando esta relación, pero también incorporará nuevas rivales románticas y acontecimientos escolares, incluyendo festivales y otras actividades que pondrán a prueba la inexperiencia sentimental de la protagonista. En cuanto a la producción, Yasushi Muroya regresará como director en Studio KAI , acompañado nuevamente por Hisashi Isogawa como asistente de dirección. Rintaro Ikeda continuará supervisando los guiones, mientras que Akari Minagawa se encargará del diseño de personajes. La primera temporada del anime se estrenó el 4 de abril de 2026 y contó con distribución internacional mediante Crunchyroll. La franquicia adapta el manga escrito e ilustrado por nonco , que comenzó a publicarse en junio de 2022 dentro de la revista Weekly Shonen Magazine de Kodansha. Cabe recordar que la producción de una segunda temporada ya había sido anunciada en junio de 2026, poco después del final de la primera entrega. Sin embargo, esta es la primera vez que se confirma su estreno para 2027 , además de presentar oficialmente a las nuevas integrantes del reparto. Por ahora, los responsables todavía no han revelado el mes exacto del estreno ni la cantidad de episodios. Tampoco se ha confirmado si Crunchyroll continuará distribuyendo la serie internacionalmente. ¿Crees que Kanan finalmente aprenderá a comportarse como una novia normal en esta segunda temporada, o veremos cómo una demonio de miles de años sigue perdiendo la compostura por algo tan sencillo como tomarse de las manos? title: What is Japan’s Yamagata soba, and do you have to go to Yamagata to eat it?
summary: Our traveling reporter has his first experience with Yamagata’s style of buckwheat noodles, but he could have eaten them much closer to home too. Fans of Japanese noodles are no doubt already aware of the regional ramen differences, such as Hokkaido’s heavy concentration of restaurants that specialize in miso broth and Fukuoka’s preference for tonkotsu […]
details: Our traveling reporter has his first experience with Yamagata’s style of buckwheat noodles, but he could have eaten them much closer to home too . Fans of Japanese noodles are no doubt already aware of the regional ramen differences, such as Hokkaido’s heavy concentration of restaurants that specialize in miso broth and Fukuoka’s preference for tonkotsu (pork stock). Different parts of Japan sometimes also do their soba/buckwheat noodles differently too, and on a recent trip to Japan’s northeastern Tohoku region our Japanese-language reporter P.K. Sanjun got to try Yamagata soba for the first time . First, a little introduction to the characteristics of Yamagata soba. While all soba noodles contain buckwheat flour, in Yamagata they use unpolished buckwheat flour, which leaves little pieces of the grain’s husk in the dough . The result is soba noodles with a darker color and more pronounced buckwheat scent, plus a coarser texture and extra-chewy consistency . Zooming in closer still, we come to the representative types of soba for different parts of Yamagata Prefecture, with the one we’re tasting today being a specific style of niku soba (“meat soba”) that originated in the town of Kahoku . In most parts of Japan, the meat that you’ll find in niku soba is strips of either pork or beef. Kahoku’s niku soba, though, uses chicken , both in strips and in thicker chashu-style cuts. The broth is made with chicken stock too , and while some connoisseurs say Yamagata niku soba is a dish/bowl best served cold, you can order it hot too, which is what Sanun did on his visit to Yamagata soba specialty restaurant Toshichi . This restaurant is actually in the city of Sendai , which is in Miyagi Prefecture, Yamagata’s neighbor to the east, but thus still within the Yamagata soba sphere of influence. The restaurant, a 15-minute walk from Sendai Station, is only open for three hours each day, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., but there was a long line of local businessmen waiting to get in when P.K. arrived (the above photo was snapped after his meal), so he had high hopes that a very good meal was awaiting him. Prices for niku soba start at 760 yen (US$4.80), but P.K. splurged for a large-size bowl for 880 yen, and he also tacked on a topping order of tempura squid tentacles , a popular accompaniment for soba in Yamagata. After a short wait, a very hearty-looking bowl of noodles was placed before P.K., with a small pile of sliced green onion at its center. He started with a sip of the broth, which had a faint gold hue to it from the chicken stock and a meaty sweetness as it splashed onto his taste buds . The noodles were thick and dark, with a speckled pattern from the bits of soba husk. They were, as promised, extremely chewy , and if they hadn’t been softened up from soaking in the hot broth, P.K. thinks his jaw would have been tired out from trying to bite through them. They were tasty, though, and very filling. P.K. has a pretty big appetite on most days, but even he had no complaints about the quantity of noodles. There’s more firmness to be found in the chicken, too . As is often the style with Yamagata soba, Toshichi uses mature chickens for its meat and broth, and while the meat isn’t tough, stringy, or otherwise low-quality, it does require some chewing. That just gives you more time to enjoy the flavor, though. And last, the tempura squid was excellent as well, giving P.K. no regrets whatsoever about asking for the extra topping. Again, this was P.K.’s first experience with Yamagata soba, and what he had specifically was one type of Yamagata soba, Kahoku-style niku soba, but he came away very impressed with how substantial-feeling and satisfying the noodles were. Lucky for him, it turns out in addition to its two Sendai locations, Toshichi also has a third branch in downtown Tokyo’s Hanzomon neighborhood , so he, or you, can enjoy a taste of Yamagata soba even if a trip up to Tohoku isn’t in your travel plans. title: Starbucks Japan unveils new Christmas Matcha Tiramisu Frappuccino
summary: Serving up the tastiest Christmas tree, with layers of powdered green tea. At this time of year in Japan, you’ll start to see Christmas trees popping up all over the place, with their green hues brightening the landscape as the days get colder and shorter. It’s not the only place you’ll be seeing green, as […]
details: Serving up the tastiest Christmas tree, with layers of powdered green tea. At this time of year in Japan, you’ll start to see Christmas trees popping up all over the place, with their green hues brightening the landscape as the days get colder and shorter. It’s not the only place you’ll be seeing green, as Starbucks Japan has just announced it will be welcoming the holiday season with a luxurious new Matcha Tiramisu Frappuccino . Taking its inspiration from the famous Italian dessert, the new Frappuccino combines rich, creamy mascarpone with the bittersweet taste of matcha, creating a layered drink with generous amounts of Japanese tea flavour. At the bottom of the cup, you’ll find a rich, concentrated matcha sauce filled with the delicious bittersweet umami notes of powdered green tea. In the middle is a Frappuccino base with an original blend of matcha powder, which, when combined with the bottom layer, is said to create a blend so tasty it’ll make matcha lovers swoon. Topped with a generous layer of mascarpone cream, to recreate the creamy layer of a traditional tiramisu, the drink is sprinkled with a light dusting of matcha powder to finish. According to Starbucks, the new Frappuccino was born from the desire to give the chain’s much-loved matcha a more festive feel, and tiramisu, with its distinctive layers of mascarpone cream, was deemed to be the perfect match for creating a special holiday drink. It certainly looks like a delicious pairing for the holiday season, and it’ll be on the menu for a limited time from 20 November, priced from 707 yen (US$4.71). title: We try Japan’s craziest energy drink…from a Street Fighter card!
summary: This new product might look like a trading card, but it’s actually an energy drink. Energy drinks usually come in bottles or cans, but right now in Japan there’s a new invention that’s blowing people’s minds. It’s a drink in a card, and at first glance, it looks exactly like an ordinary trading card, complete […]
details: This new product might look like a trading card, but it’s actually an energy drink. Energy drinks usually come in bottles or cans, but right now in Japan there’s a new invention that’s blowing people’s minds. It’s a drink in a card , and at first glance, it looks exactly like an ordinary trading card, complete with Street Fighter characters , but they’re actually designed for you to put your lips on, so you can take a sip and get an energy hit, just like a character replenishing their HP. Created by UHA Mikakuto, this unusual product goes by the official name ENERGY ARTS , and it was recently ranked fifth in Nikkei Trendy’s Top 30 Hit Predictions for 2027 . At the moment, it’s such a rare product that it can only be purchased online, and as we were curious to find out how it works, our reporter Yayoi Saginomiya ordered a box from Amazon to test it out in person. When her package arrived, Yayoi was surprised at how compact it was, with the box, containing 10 individual cards, being just a little bigger than the palm of her hand. As a collaboration product with the popular fighting game Street Fighter 6 , each individual packet features a selection from 24 exclusive designs: 23 different characters plus one group illustration . The designs are included at random, so Yayoi opened her 10 packets to see what she got, and she was happy to find that the only duplicate in her pack was the group illustration. Now it was time to give it a try, and since her son was at home when the package arrived, she decided to let him try one to get his verdict as well. All you have to do to drink this card is hold it vertically with the plain white side (the side without the design) facing you, then bring it up to your mouth. Fold it with one hand, and… ▼ …take a sip! Both Yayoi and her son couldn’t quite believe it when a little squirt of liquid released itself from the card straight into their mouths. It was easy to suck up, and although it might take a little practice the first few times, if you look closely at the white side, you’ll see a cross-shaped slit that shows you exactly where to fold it. Each packet contains just 12 millilitres (0.4 ounces) of liquid, and according to the manufacturer, one of its major selling points is the fact that you can drink it in just 0.5 seconds . It’s convenient when you’re busy, and there’s no need to worry about leaving any unfinished drink behind. However, after trying it in person, Yayoi found there was one issue she couldn’t overlook: the taste . If she’s being honest, it didn’t taste particularly good – it had a highly concentrated energy drink flavour, with a slightly medicinal aftertaste. That said, it’s certainly not undrinkable, so for a lot of people, and gamers in particular, it won’t be a dealbreaker. Yayoi’s son actually liked it and enthusiastically declared it delicious, so the taste is ultimately a matter of personal preference. ▼ Either way, it’s incredibly thin and compact, making it easy to slip into a suit pocket, which is what Yayoi’s husband chose to do. ▼ Or you can tuck it away inside a bag or pouch for times when you need an instant boost. The Street Fighter designs make these a must-have for fans of the franchise, and although Yayoi isn’t particularly familiar with the series or its characters, even she got a kick out of the cards. While the cards are currently only available online, through sites like the official UHA Mikakuto online store, Amazon and Rakuten, Yayoi reckons their popularity might just lead to a wider release in future. Yayoi bought her box on Amazon for 3,383 yen (US$22), which works out to almost 340 yen per packet. While that might be a dealbreaker for some people, as it’s pretty pricey for a 12-millilitre energy drink, for gamers and fans of the franchise, the chance to drink from a Street Fighter card is a priceless experience. title: SmaGO “smart trash cans” installed within the grounds of Kyoto’s Kiyomizudera
summary: They’re the first solar-powered, smart trash cans to be installed within the grounds of a temple or shrine anywhere in Japan. Recently, Japan has been in the midst of a refuse revolution in the way that it collects and transports trash. As a country with very few public trash cans that’s also experiencing waves of […]
details: They’re the first solar-powered, smart trash cans to be installed within the grounds of a temple or shrine anywhere in Japan. Recently, Japan has been in the midst of a refuse revolution in the way that it collects and transports trash. As a country with very few public trash cans that’s also experiencing waves of overtourism in many cities , there’s no time to waste in tackling the problem of what to do with the very real and very over-capacity volume of waste in many urban areas. One of the most promising solutions is a series of solar-powered, smart trash cans called “SmaGO” by Japanese company Forcetec that have hit the scene in 80 different locations around the country as of this writing. Research shows that they’ve already been making an impact by reducing the frequency of trash collection times by about 70 percent in Tokyo’s Omotesando/Harajuku shopping district and by reducing litter–apart from cigarette butts–by 90 percent in Osaka’s Dotonburi canal area. Now, they’re also found in 19 areas of Japan’s ancient capital of Kyoto City –and in a first for the whole country, directly within the actual grounds of a temple or shrine. Actually, UNESCO World Heritage Site Kiyomizudera, a temple of the Shingon Sect of Buddhism, was constructed before the capital even moved to modern-day Kyoto in 794 CE. It’s probably not the first place you’d think of to host a futuristic-sounding receptacle, but a line of SmaGO trash cans is now gracing its grounds inside of the Niomon Gate. Kiyomizudera easily makes it into the top three most popular attractions for most visitors to Kyoto with its wide balcony offering sweeping views of the surrounding scenery year-round. During peak foliage season in the fall, it can even see up to 20,000-30,000 visitors per day. Up until now, the temple was struggling to accommodate the sheer volume of trash deposited in its bins despite sanitation workers emptying them around four times per day. The situation was dire enough that the religious corporation behind the temple gladly partnered with Forcetec to install the new bins, which have a function to automatically compress the accumulated trash to about one-fifth of its original volume . Workers are able to remotely check the status via a cloud network to optimize the time of removal, which is slated to be reduced to only once per day. The SmaGO trash cans are also designed to promote recycling for glass bottles, cans, and plastic bottles and to make Japan’s somewhat complicated trash-sorting rules more visible. Color-coded labels with pictures and text in both Japanese and English on the cans should reduce barriers for foreign visitors as well. Furthermore, one of the new receptacles is specifically intended for leftover beverages. A mechanism inside it separates bottles from the liquid and funnels the latter directly into a sewage pipe. As the shopping streets leading up to Kiyomizudera are packed with places to grab a quick bite to eat or drink while walking, this new one should help visitors dispose of any unwanted refreshment while mitigating the odor and leakage. Time will tell whether the SmartGo smart trash cans make more than just a literal dent in the trash in Japan’s heavily touristed areas, even within sacred grounds. With several groups of them installed in Tokyo’s Akihabara electronics district just one week ago, it looks like the future is (not) full of wasted potential after all. You know, Studio Ghibli and Uniqlo , Pokémon and manga artist Tetsuo Hara , Hello Kitty and soft, pillowy toilet paper , those sorts of combinations. But while KFC Japan is an organization most people have no problem with, support is much less universal for their latest creative partner: Doctor Doom . 【重要なお知らせ】 この度KFCは、ドゥームズデイ対策の一環として、マーベル最新のヴィラン、ドクター・ドゥーム氏との契約締結を完了いたしましたので、ここにお知らせいたします。… pic.twitter.com/mAmL9mp2qf — ケンタッキーフライドチキン (@KFC_jp) November 16, 2026 “KFC has entered into a contract with Dr. Doom” says KFC Japan in announcing their joint venture with the Marvel Comics supervillain. “KFC is devoted to upholding its side of the contract by continuing to fry up delicious chicken and offer it with friendly customer service even as Doomsday approaches.” The doctor and the colonel are working together in the runup to the theatrical premiere of Avengers: Doomsday , the long-awaited next chapter in the Marvel Cinematic Universe’s most popular franchise. Starting November 25, KFC Japan will be serving the Double Doom Burger . This new version of the chain’s Double Down “sandwich” continues its tradition of replacing the bread with boneless Original Recipe chicken cutlets . Those cutlets are wrapped around a hash brown patty with slices of cheese on either side, and the Double Doom adds in a Dr. Doom-like green Smokey Green Mayo made with garlic, honey, and lime, plus some sinister-sounding “Doom Cola Sauce.” Bundled with fries and a drink, the 1,750-yen (US$11) Double Doom Burger Set will be available in limited quantities at 56 KFC Japan branches. ▼ The full list of branches can be found here , with the ones Tokyo travelers are most likely to find themselves near being KFC Japan’s Ikebukuro Nishiguchi, Ginza INZ, and Shinjuku Toho Building locations. Meanwhile, from November 25 all KFC Japan branches will be offering the Doom Bucket (called the “Doom Barrel” in Japanese). This is, thankfully, not a bucket of misfortune, but a bucket of chicken containing two pieces of Original Recipe and a Colonel’s Crispy boneless chicken tender. The crossover condiments here are Smokey Green Mayo dipping sauce and a packet of Lime and Smoked Chili Doom Seasoning powder , and once again you get fries on the side, as part of the 1,650-yen set. Diners buying either of the Dr. Doom-themed items will receive a Doomsday sticker with a QR code on the back , which they can use to be entered for a chance to win one of four prizes, either a KFC/Dr. Doom jacket, sweatshirt, cap, or one of five figures of KFC founder Colonel Sanders cosplaying as characters who appear in the movie . ▼ Colonel Sanders Gambit makes sense, since they share Southern roots. Though both menu items are officially scheduled for sale between November 25 and December 17, they’re also both listed as limited-quantity, so availability might not stretch all the way to the end of that period. For those who don’t want to miss this chance to dine like Doom, the Double Doom Burger Set and Doom Barrel can be reserved through KFC Japan’s website or mobile app starting November 20 at 6 a.m. Related: KFC Japan Source: KFC Japan Top image: KFC Japan Insert images: Twitter/KFC_jp , KFC Japan ( 1 , 2 ) ● Want to hear about SoraNews24’s latest articles as soon as they’re published? title: Tommy Lee Jones becomes Pikachu in Japan for Suntory
summary: Alien Jones turns his attention to Pokémon. Among Hollywood celebrities, Tommy Lee Jones has always had an old-fashioned, no-nonsense persona. His aura of down-to-earth unpretentiousness makes him the kind of guy who could, conceivably, reach for Suntory’s Boss canned coffee when he’s craving caffeinated refreshment, as the brand is known for being good-tasting without needing […]
details: Alien Jones turns his attention to Pokémon . Among Hollywood celebrities, Tommy Lee Jones has always had an old-fashioned, no-nonsense persona. His aura of down-to-earth unpretentiousness makes him the kind of guy who could, conceivably, reach for Suntory’s Boss canned coffee when he’s craving caffeinated refreshment, as the brand is known for being good-tasting without needing to resort to outlandish special flavors. Of course, that atmosphere of solemn dignity is slightly diluted in Jones’ latest ads for Boss, in which the 80-year-old veteran actor dresses as Pikachu . The unexpected outfit comes as part of Boss’ collaboration with the 30th anniversary celebration of the Pokémon franchise . Jones has been a regular pitchman for Boss for many years, one of the few Hollywood celebrities to stick around with a regular marketing deal in Japan after many of his brethren started avoiding such work, as Internet video-sharing platforms mean such silly side projects can no longer be limited to viewers in Japan only like they were in the 1980s and ‘90s. Not only is Jones unconcerned about being laughed at, that’s arguably the entire point of his ads for Boss, in which he portrays “Alien Jones,” a stern-faced extraterrestrial who comes to earth to observe hard-working humans in their natural environments. Suntory is currently running a promotion in which customers who buy a six-pack of Boss coffee between now and January 31 have a chance of winning a jacket with the Boss logo and the Pokémon 30th anniversary emblem. So to get into the spirit, Alien Jones is doing a little light Pikachu cosplay. He’s also apparently expanded his observational operations to include Pokémon species, such as in this short video where he learns about Psyduck . The Pokémon called Psyduck. Similarly to the people living on this planet, when it feels excessive stress it develops an escalating headache, and cradles its head in response. There is a sense of satisfaction in seeing it overwhelm its surroundings with its strong psychic powers. With Suntory being one of Japan’s biggest beverage makers, we’ll probably be seeing the Pikachu Tommy Lee Jones popping up on posters and signboards at various stores in Japan, but if you want to be sure of spotting him, Suntory will be taking over the Ueno Canvas and adjacent concourse outside the Chuo Gate of Ueno Station in Tokyo from now until November 22 so that their Poké-fied alien can greet travelers in large-scale style. title: Studio Ghibli and Uniqlo reveal brand-new T-shirt collaboration [Pics]
summary: Once again coming to fans around the world, except in Japan. Uniqlo is no stranger to collaborations with Japan’s most beloved anime and manga franchises, so it seems only natural that they periodically team up with Studio Ghibli. The two have recently revealed that they’re ready for a brand-new batch of Ghibli UT Graphic T-shirts, […]
details: Once again coming to fans around the world, except in Japan . Uniqlo is no stranger to collaborations with Japan’s most beloved anime and manga franchises , so it seems only natural that they periodically team up with Studio Ghibli . The two have recently revealed that they’re ready for a brand-new batch of Ghibli UT Graphic T-shirts , with veteran anime film producer Toshio Suzuki even personally creating one of the featured illustrations. Uniqlo describes this latest chapter of their partnership with: The theme of the collection is “LIVE FOR TODAY, MY DEAR.” The UT designs feature iconic Studio Ghibli works, including photos taken by Thai artist Kanyada at the Ghibli Museum, Mitaka, new illustrations, and poster art used in exhibitions. The collection expresses the joy of cherishing each day and the rich worlds of Studio Ghibli’s works. The collection consists of five adult-size T-shirts , and the one that fans’ eyes are probably going to immediately lock on to is this one, with the theme printed on the chest and a whole bunch of Ghibli characters flying and frolicking on the back . Suzuki, who drew this illustration himself, says that the somewhat bewildered-looking pig standing next to Spirited Away’s No Name is meant to be his portrait of fellow Studio Ghibli co-founder Hayao Miyazaki , who often depicts himself as a pig in doodles. ▼ Suzuki also says he rushed through the drawing of little witch Kiki, but isn’t entirely unsatisfied with how it turned out. Though you can find passionate fans of almost any Ghibli work, Totoro remains the most immediately recognizable symbol of the studio, so next we have a My Neighbor Totoro tee, with several different versions of the forest spirit lounging about, and even an appearance by the Catbus . ▼ Front ▼ Back Howl’s Moving Castle is the inspiration for the last of the double-sided designs, with Calcifer and deceptively important Turnip Head on the front… …and Heen sleepily, but doggedly, watching your back. Switching over to the shirts that only feature artwork on the front, they still have plenty of illustrative impact, with a slew of Soot Sprites reminding us of places “where a world of mystery still lives on”… …and Castle in the Sky/Laputa’s Robot Soldier making sure no one forgets which Ghibli film it hails from. There are also four kids-size shirts , two of which are alternate versions of the Suzuki-illustrated Ghibli cast group shot and My Neighbor Totoro , and the other two being unique Howl’s Moving Castle and Spirited Away designs. In what’s become a puzzling pattern, though, once again the Ghibli Uniqlo collection will be available internationally, but not in Japan . It’s not clear why Japan is always excluded from the collaboration, but that’s been the case for years now, and doesn’t seem likely to change anytime soon. Prices and release dates vary by region, with Uniqlo stores and online shops operating in Malaysia, Thailand, and Taiwan offering them from December 14 . European Uniqlo shops, including those in the U.K. and Spain, will have theirs on January 21 , and Uniqlo U.S.A. has them listed as “arriving late January.” Source: Uniqlo Top image: Uniqlo Insert images: Uniqlo ( 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 ) ● Want to hear about SoraNews24’s latest articles as soon as they’re published? title: Are the viral fries at De Frites Staan Harajuku really worth the hype?
summary: We find out what a local Japanese woman thinks of the Belgian fries obsession in Tokyo. Our reporter Natsuki Gojo prides herself on her willpower, as she has the strength to say no to a lot of things. One of the few things she can’t say no to, however, is potato chips, and she likes […]
details: We find out what a local Japanese woman thinks of the Belgian fries obsession in Tokyo. Our reporter Natsuki Gojo prides herself on her willpower, as she has the strength to say no to a lot of things. One of the few things she can’t say no to, however, is potato chips, and she likes them so much that sometimes she gets an overwhelming craving for them. It was only a matter of time before the algorithm caught on to Natsuki’s weak spot, so her feed recently became flooded with chip recommendations, and one that caught her eye was a post that sang the praises of the fries at De Frites Staan Harajuku . This specialty shop serves frites , the style of French fries popular in Belgium and France, which are thick-cut and served in a cone, and they looked so good that she knew right away that she had to go and try them. According to the store’s official Instagram account, dine-in customers can’t order fries on their own, so if you want to try just the fries, you’ll need to order takeout, and if you’re an early bird like Natsuki, it’s good to note that takeout orders start 30 minutes after the store opens. Since she wanted to focus entirely on enjoying the frites, she decided to go with takeout, and from the two sizes available – small and regular – she ordered the small size for 1,188 yen (US$7.90). There are both free and paid dipping sauces available, and Natsuki decided to try the popular Mayonnaise & Truffle sauce , which costs an additional 270 yen. After a short wait outside the store, Natsuki’s number was called and she was handed the most stylish-looking fries she’d ever seen. Both the sauce and the potatoes were presented beautifully, sitting nicely in the bright red cone as if they were just waiting for their close-up. Impressed by their beauty, Natsuki was now keen to see if they tasted as good as they looked. First, she decided to try the fries on their own, without any of the dipping sauce. Freshly fried and piping hot, these fries were like nothing she’d ever tasted before. Not only did they have an incredibly crispy exterior and a wonderfully light texture but the inside remained surprisingly fluffy and soft. She could also taste the lovely aroma of the potato skins, which were more than just a supporting act – they were the star of the show. Next, she dipped the chips into the Mayonnaise & Truffle sauce, and they were just as delicious. The rich creaminess of the mayonnaise paired beautifully with the potatoes, while the mushroom-like aroma of the truffle added a lovely extra dimension that made the combination seriously moreish. At this point, she was so enraptured by the frites that she didn’t want the experience to end, but at the same time, she wanted to eat them all while they were still piping hot. It was a wonderfully delicious dilemma. The only drawback to the frites was how messy her hands got when eating them with the dipping sauce. There was so much sauce that, as she worked her way through them, she simply resigned herself to having saucy fingers, as they were too delicious for her to stop eating them. There were paper napkins at the counter, but if you’re getting takeaway, Natsuki recommends bringing a small pack of wet wipes with you so you can fully enjoy the experience. It’s now been several days since she tried the frites, and Natsuki still can’t get the memory of the wonderfully crispy-outside, fluffy-inside texture out of her mind. Even her friend who went along with her has been messaging her to ask when they can go for another visit, so it’s safe to say that these viral frites really are worth the hype. So next time you’re exploring the tight alleyways and bright storefronts of Harajuku, be sure to stop and refuel at De Frites Staan…but be aware that you might wind up dreaming about their deliciousness for days afterwards. title: Complaints of bar scams from foreign tourists in Tokyo’s Shinjuku triple compared to last year
summary: Japan’s tourism landscape keeps changing, but Kabukicho stays the same. Once upon a time, there were plans to build a kabuki theater in Tokyo’s Shinjuku Ward, and this caused a section of it to be preemptively named Kabukicho, meaning, more or less, “Kabuki town.” The name stuck, but construction of the theater was later cancelled, […]
details: Japan’s tourism landscape keeps changing, but Kabukicho stays the same . Once upon a time, there were plans to build a kabuki theater in Tokyo’s Shinjuku Ward , and this caused a section of it to be preemptively named Kabukicho , meaning, more or less, “Kabuki town.” The name stuck, but construction of the theater was later cancelled, and instead Kabukicho (pictured above) became one of the densest concentrations of bars, pubs, and host/hostess clubs in Japan . Whether that outcome is something to be lamented or celebrated depends on the relative values one personally assigns to classical stage arts, liquid refreshment, and compensated companionship. I think we can pretty much all agree, though, that it’s unfortunate that Kabukicho has also become a major source of complaints about bars running scams to rip off customers, and it appears that the number of foreign tourists getting caught in such schemes has been rapidly rising . Between January and October of this year, the Tokyo Metropolitan Police’s Shinjuku Precinct, whose jurisdiction includes Kabukicho, has received approximately 240 complaints from foreign tourists about being ripped off at bars located within the ward. This is roughly three times the number of complaints received for the same period in 2025 . A common pattern in the complaints is tourists being approached on the street by a barker, called a kyakuhiki /“customer puller” in Japanese. The barker will then lead the tourists to the bar, and when the bill is being settled at the end of the evening, the bar adds on additional charges without the customers’ knowledge or consent . Other textbook scams that ripoff bars have been known to run include exorbitant prices for otoshi (a small appetizer served upon seating at Japanese pubs) and tacking on shady, vaguely defined service or seating charges . In the case of host/hostess clubs, where the customer is required to pay both for their own food and drink as well as their companion’s, unscrupulous establishments may sneak extra orders and services onto the bill and say they were at the request of the host/hostess, even if the customer did not agree to them. In total, the Shinjuku Precinct has received around 340 complaints of bar ripoffs within the ward so far this year, with the claimed damages coming to a total of roughly 390 million yen (US$2.45 million). That’s nearly triple the amount for the entire year of 2025, 140 million yen. In looking through the complaints, the Tokyo Metropolitan Police say they’ve noticed a pattern of African kyakuhiki specifically targeting foreign tourists , whose lack of familiarity with Japanese bar industry standard practices might make them easier to trick. As part of a crackdown, on November 11 the police arrested a 62-year-old Nigerian resident of Japan on charges of running an unlicensed bar in Kabukicho. With roughly 70 percent of the complaints regarding ripoff bars coming from foreign tourists, it’s difficult to say whether such scams as a whole are becoming more common, or if Japan’s ongoing inbound foreign tourism boom simply means that there are more potential victims who are more likely to go to the police with grievances. Kabukicho being filled with ripoff bars has long been common knowledge among Japanese natives and the country’s expat population, and with some of the schemes they pull being dishonest but not technically illegal, there’s a certain amount of embarrassment involved in admitting that you got tricked, likely in part due to lowered defenses because you were some combination of drunk and horny. So what can you do to protect yourself? For starters, it’s best to exercise caution with kyakuhiki. Because of their association with ripoff joints, it’s become uncommon for businesses that are on the up and up to dispatch them much farther than maybe the front entrance of their establishment. The longer the march a kyakuhiki takes you on, the more likely it is that something fishy is going to happen, since that distance and disorientation (i.e. isolation and confusion) is often part of the setup. Geeting upfront information about service charges is also advisable if you’re not used to Japan’s bar scene, and the following phrases are good to know . ● Otoshi dai wa ikura desu ka ? / How much does the otoshi cost? ● Teburu chaji wa arimasu ka ? / Is there a table charge? ● Sekiryo wa arimasu ka ? / Is there a seating charge? ● Sabisu chaji wa arimasu ka ? / Is there a service charge? If you want to be extra cautious, sticking to established chain pubs and bars is also an effective way to avoid scams. That’s not to say scams are common among independent establishments, but the large chains’ need to comply with all laws and regulations in order to not bring down their entire business group means that they can pretty much always be trusted not to rip you off. And finally, don’t forget that it’s not just official kyakuhiki who try to lure victims into ripoff schemes, so should you meet an attractive stranger who seems unusually fixated on having a drink with you at a particular but unremarkable bar , that’s also probably a sign that bad things are afoot. title: Nara deer send record number of people to hospital, over 70 percent of patients are foreigners
summary: Just because Nara’s deer are usually cute and calm doesn’t mean they’re not still wild animals who will mess you up if you give them a reason to. For anyone with the city of Nara on their Japan travel itinerary, Nara Park, with its herds of deer that roam freely across its grounds, is a […]
details: Just because Nara’s deer are usually cute and calm doesn’t mean they’re not still wild animals who will mess you up if you give them a reason to . For anyone with the city of Nara on their Japan travel itinerary, Nara Park , with its herds of deer that roam freely across its grounds, is a must-visit. Unfortunately, for some tourists the hospital has become a must-visit in Nara too, as this year has seen a record-setting number of people taken by ambulance to Nara Municipal Hospital for treatment for deer-induced injuries, with the majority being foreign visitors . To recap, Nara’s deer are considered messengers of the gods under Shinto belief, and so they’re given more or less free reign to go wherever they want within the park. They’ve become very accustomed to human visitors and don’t scatter when people come near, and posing for pictures with the animals and feeding them some special deer cracker snacks purchased from venders in and around the park have become the top tourist activities in the town. However, it’s important to remember that Nara’s deer are not domesticated . Despite their comparative comfort mingling with humans, they are still wild animals, and injuries can occur if proper caution isn’t exercised when interacting with them. In addition to biting and butting, the deers’ antlers can be incredibly sharp, with a near knife-like keenness to them, experts warn . They can become particularly aggressive around people who are carrying deer crackers, sometimes even following them throughout the park if they know the person hasn’t yet handed out the entire pack of treats. ▼ An elderly woman can be seen in this video describing how deer have nipped at her coat pockets if they think she still has deer crackers on her. ▼ The man seen at the start of this video also talks about having been bit on the leg by a Nara deer. As of November 5, Nara Municipal Hospital reports having received 51 patients who were transported by ambulance to the facility for treatment for deer-induced injuries . This tops last year’s 46 patients and 2024’s 45, both of which were themselves records, which were themselves proportionally huge increases from previous years. Out of the 51 patients so far this year, over 70 percent have been foreigners. ● Patients taken by ambulance to Nara Municipal Hospital for deer-induced injuries 2026 (through November 5): 51 2025: 46 2024: 45 2023: 23 2022: 11 2021: 7 2020: 10 2019: 24 2018: 15 2017: 15 As for what’s causing the increase in injuries, the Nara administration is citing increases in both the number of visitors to Nara Park as well as the number of deer living within it . It’s worth noting that the ratio of injuries to visitors hasn’t gone up, at least not compared to five years ago. In 2021, when Japan still had several international tourism-limiting pandemic protocols in place, Nara Park received around 46,000 foreign visitors. In 2025, that number grew to more than 3.5 million, so the percentage of visitors injured by deer has certainly decreased. That said, such statistics will be of little comfort to anyone who does need to be taken to the hospital after an unfortunate altercation with a deer, and the Nara Deer Preservation Society cautions against getting too close to or petting deer that don’t seem receptive to such advances. They also warn against teasing deer by holding out crackers as if they’re being offered, then pulling them back without actually giving them to the animals . Finally, autumn is a time of year when visitors should be especially cautious, they add, as it’s mating season, when males can become particularly aggressive and territorial, so it’s advisable to give them extra space, especially if you see two male deer who are beefing with each other.
